For as eight times nine [72], the variety of the world’s mouth <note>The 72 languages/nations of the earth</note> is spoken of,
And from here, nine [choirs of angels]... **remain in the blessed light**.
Of spirits, it is given that the Creator may fulfill the eighth [age] <note>The "Eighth Day" signifies eternity or the resurrection</note>.
He wishes to rightly close the ages with an end on this day.
For He consumed all the **crimes** of the world in Himself,
The Creator, by suffering in the flame-vomiting heat of the Cross.
But nevertheless, the divine [nature] shone out from the side of the flesh;
Nature brought forth the **shining** <note>original: "obrium," likely referring to refined gold or pure light</note> laws and the rising [of light].
Indeed, He made His beloved law in the order of the Cross,
Rightly light and sweet, given as a gift for **climbing** <note>to heaven</note>.

### FO. XLIII. ###

## BOOK ONE ##

# Figure XXI. On the number seventy-two and its significations. #

->The true law of God must also be **won** by the blessed lot<-
->Behold the Cross of Christ, by which the world is released from wrath,<-
->It is led toward life and reaches the harbor of rest,<-
->After the fall of the first earth-born man <note>original: *aruigenæ primi*. This refers to Adam, the first man created from the earth</note>, who was himself shipwrecked.<-
For because harmful death conquered through the forbidden tree,
And had consumed all the human race with savage **greed**,
It was so that He might lift them from the jaws of death through this wood <note>The Cross is traditionally viewed as the "antitype" or corrective to the Tree of Knowledge in Eden</note>:
By the law of the Cross, it pleased the Restorer to place the stake
Against the dire one; and that which the atrocious enemy had swallowed in his **moist** belly,
He should vomit forth <note>original: *euomeret*. A vivid image of the Harrowing of Hell, where death is forced to release the souls of the righteous</note>, and thus pay the penalties for his debts:
That which the savage thief wickedly invaded and snatched away as dominion,
God, the author of the Testaments, wished to signify in **various** ways in the written teachings;
He foretold the work of the Cross itself,
The Almighty taught it, and confesses that He has fulfilled it.
The almighty Cross **from here** therefore shows itself entirely gleaming,
To be received into the light; it provides on **a dedicated path**
**Rightly** a beacon <note>original: *faros*. Referring to the Pharos or lighthouse, guiding the faithful</note> to the righteous, testifying to itself through all the air:
It calls the nations and peoples to the high stars,
It marks those who are rescued, and knows they are eager through the prayer of the night
To do no small thing; hence it leads to the heights of the kingdom,
Once the enemy is expelled, the Cross is victorious, and it does not fail in its skill,
But ruling as the sole master of the human race, it presents miracles,
It makes all kingdoms serve it because of its gifts—
Devout, and peaceful, gentle, quiet, and redeemed:
Behold, however many languages the world has, and laws of speech <note>The number seventy-two was traditionally the number of languages created at the Tower of Babel</note>,
By this number it marks the entrance for those coming,
And the Savior opens this path for His disciples.
For the mouth of the world is said to vary by **eight times nine** <note>72</note>,
And hence he gives nine remainders in the light;
The eighth is given of the blessed spirits, so that the Creator might wish
To fulfill creation rightly on this day, and close the ages at the end.
For the Creator, by suffering, consumed all the sins of the world
In that very **flame-vomiting** <note>original: *flammiuomo*. A rare and powerful term suggesting the intense, purifying heat of divine love/judgment</note> heat of the Cross,
But yet, while He suffered in His flesh, His divine
Nature shone back in the inscription, and brought forth a sober rising:
Truly He made His law beloved through the order of the Cross,
By right light, sweet, and rich with the gift of ascending.

### FO. XLIII. ###

# EXPLANATION. #

<meta>catchword: Every (original: Omnis)</meta>

One must understand, therefore, that this figure is full of mystery. In it, the number seventy-two <note>LXXII</note> is demonstrated through four heptagons <note>seven-sided polygons</note>. It is a widely held and true opinion that the languages of the nations were divided according to this plurality <note>According to medieval tradition based on Genesis 10, there were 72 nations and 72 distinct languages created at the Tower of Babel</note>, and there is no doubt that the canonical books of the Old and New Testaments are encompassed within this sum. The Lord himself also designated seventy-two disciples, in addition to the twelve Apostles, and sent them in pairs before his face into every place and city where he himself was to come. He did this so that the number of designated disciples might correspond to the multitude of nations and the division of languages, to the end that all nations might receive the light of faith and deserve to be sharers in the grace of Christ. Therefore, just as the entire world is traversed and illuminated in twenty-four hours, so the mystery of illuminating the world through the Gospel of the Trinity is suggested in the seventy-two disciples. For twenty-four times three is seventy-two <note>original: *Vicies enim quater terni septuagies dipondius*. This is a complex way of calculating 24 x 3 = 72</note>.

But this distribution is aptly assigned to the figure of the Holy Cross, because through it, by the dispensation of Christ’s <term>sacraments</term> <note>the sacred rites of the Church, such as Baptism and the Eucharist</note>, the whole world is glorified. The Cross itself denotes this logic of the mystery in the four heptagons: because it dispenses divine <term>charismata</term> <note>spiritual gifts or graces</note> through the four books of the Holy Gospel across the four quarters of the world. Within both paths—that is, in the vertical beam and the transverse beam—it shows "six times six" <note>36</note> through two heptagons. This indicates clearly enough to us that every perfection comes to us through the Cross, whether in the long-suffering of hope, the breadth of charity, the perseverance of good action, or the height of contemplation. In its entirety, it contains "eight times nine" multiplied within itself; it teaches that from all nations, through the number eight—which signifies the resurrection of bodies—the elect of God reach the increase of the nine orders of Angels.

O truly good and truly holy Cross of Christ, who can rightly recount you in full? Or who can worthily praise you? You are the pious revealer of heavenly secrets, the sacred guardian of the mysteries of God, and the fitting dispenser of the sacraments of Christ. In you, the Angels behold their joys accumulated; in you, humans recognize the laws of their salvation; in you, the inhabitants of the underworld perceive the just retribution for their deceit. You are equal to all, good to all, just to all. You renew the past, illuminate the present, and foretell the future. You seek the lost, find what was sought, and guard what is found; you restore the fallen, fortify the restored, and direct the fortified onto the path of peace.

You are indeed the victory of the eternal King, the joy of the heavenly host, and the power of those born of earth. You are the remission of sins, the display of piety, and the increase of merits; the remedy for the sick, the help for the laboring, and the refreshment for the weary; the safety of the healthy, the serenity of the peaceful, and the happiness of the fortunate. You, O Cross, are the medicine healing the sick, the joy consoling the sorrowful, the health gladdening those in pain, the standing of those who believe rightly, the firmness of those who work well, and the blessedness of those who persevere properly. 

Holy, pious, good, just, kind, rational, praiseworthy, venerable, lovable, strong, sweet, gentle, wise, patient, powerful. Therefore, whatever can be worthily thought in the heart concerning our redemption, or whatever the tongue can rightly speak, all things can most becomingly be adapted to your praise. For whatever is praised in you is credited to Christ the King, who was crucified upon you; and whatever honor is given to Christ refers back to the reverence of the Father most high, whose only-begotten Son He is. Of Him, Truth itself <note>Jesus Christ</note> testifies in the Gospel: *He who receives me,* He says, *receives Him who sent me.* And likewise: *He who spurns me, spurns Him who sent me, and he who does not honor the Son, does not honor the Father.*

He concludes with a rhythmic, litany-like prayer of praise to the Cross as the source of all virtues and the instrument of salvation.</summary>

For indeed, everyone who denies the Son does not have the Father; but he who acknowledges the Son has the Father as well. <note>original: "Omnis quippe qui negat filium, nec patrem habet: qui autem confitetur filium, & patrem habet." A paraphrase of 1 John 2:23.</note> Together with the Holy Spirit, their majesty is one, their power is one, as are their honor and glory for eternal ages. According to the true opinion, the languages of the nations were divided according to this plurality <note>a reference to the 72 nations and languages traditionally believed to have emerged after the Tower of Babel</note>, and there is no doubt that the canonical books of the Old and New Testaments are contained within this sum. For whatever is praised in you is attributed to Christ the King crucified upon you; and whatever honor is given to Christ refers back to the reverence of the Most High Father, whose only-begotten Son he is, to which Truth itself testifies in the Gospel:

> He who receives me, he says, receives him who sent me. ### **EXPLANATION.**
<meta>catchword: Every</meta>

Therefore, one must understand that this figure is full of mystery. Within it, the number 72 is demonstrated through four heptagons <note>seven-sided polygons</note>. It is a true and established opinion that the languages of the nations were divided according to this same number <note>The tradition of 72 nations and languages stems from the Table of Nations in Genesis 10</note>, and there is no doubt that the canonical books of the Old and New Testaments are contained within this sum. Furthermore, the Lord himself designated 72 other disciples—besides the twelve Apostles—and sent them out in pairs before him into every place and city where he himself was to come. He did this so that the number of designated disciples would harmonize with the multitude of nations and the division of languages, ensuring that all peoples might perceive the light of faith and deserve to be sharers in the grace of Christ.

Just as the entire world is traversed and illuminated in 24 hours, so too is the mystery of illuminating the world through the Gospel of the Trinity signaled in the 72 disciples. For three times 24 is 72 <note>original: "Vicies enim quater terni septuagies dipondius"</note>. This distribution is aptly assigned to the figure of the Holy Cross, because through the cross, in the dispensation of the sacraments of Christ, the whole world is glorified. The cross itself, in these four heptagons, marks this mystical logic: it dispenses divine gifts through the four corners of the world via the four books of the Holy Gospel.

The cross shows a "six-times-six" <note>36</note> arrangement through two heptagons in each path—that is, in the vertical path that goes upward and the transverse path that goes across. This sufficiently signals to us that every perfection comes to us through the cross, whether in the long-suffering of hope, the breadth of charity, perseverance in good action, or the height of contemplation. The cross contains within itself the number nine multiplied eight times <note>8 x 9 = 72</note>; this teaches that God’s elect from all nations arrive at the increase of the nine orders of Angels through the number eight—which signifies the resurrection of bodies <note>In Christian numerology, 8 represents the "eighth day" of Resurrection and new beginnings</note>.

O truly good and truly holy Cross of Christ! Who can rightly tell your whole story? Or who can praise you worthily? You are the pious revealer of heavenly secrets; you are the sacred guardian of the mysteries of God; and you are the fit dispenser of the sacraments of Christ. In you, the Angels behold their joys multiplied; in you, humanity recognizes the laws of its salvation; in you, the dwellers of the underworld perceive the just retribution for their deceit. 

You are equal to all, good to all, and just to all. You renew the past, illustrate the present, and foretell the future. You seek the lost, find what was sought, and guard what was found. You restore the fallen, fortify those who are restored, and direct the fortified into the way of peace. You are indeed the victory of the eternal King, the joy of the heavenly host, and the power of those born of earth. You are the remission of sins, the manifestation of piety, the increase of merits, the remedy for the weak, the help of those who labor, the refreshment of the weary, the safety of the healthy, the serenity of the quiet, and the happiness of the fortunate. 

You, O Cross, are the medicine healing the sick, the joy consoling the sorrowful, the health making the grieving glad. You are the standing-ground of those who believe rightly, the firmness of those who work well, and the bliss of those who persevere properly. 

Holy, pious, good, just, kind, rational, laudable, venerable, lovely, strong, sweet, mild, wise, patient, and powerful. 

Therefore, whatever can be worthily thought in the heart regarding our redemption, or whatever the tongue can rightly speak, all can be most fittingly applied to your praise. For whatever is praised in you is credited to Christ the King who was crucified upon you; and whatever honor is given to Christ is referred back to the reverence of the Highest Father, whose only-begotten Son he is. Of this, Truth itself testifies in the Gospel:

> "Whoever receives me," he says, "receives him who sent me." And likewise: "Whoever despises me, despises him who sent me; and whoever does not honor the Son, does not honor the Father." <note>A synthesis of Matthew 10:40 and Luke 10:16</note>

### BOOK ONE.

FO.XLV.

<margin>9</margin>
Christ is my love and my vow, He who gives these holy gifts
Of song; He is the reward, He is the way, the faithful portion of rest:
Who, approving all good things by His power, rightly bestows
Such great and such many gifts upon His servants; and to these
The merciful Creator encourages all, piously promising that they
Can now obtain the citadel of the pole <note>original: "poli"; here referring to the heavens or the celestial sphere</note>, the scepters, and high kingdoms,
If hope and firm faith in the Most High are present, and if here
Chaste love holily desires those things; nor does the lost man, remembering these words, love [evil].
Indeed, coming here to the world with a joyful striving <note>original: "lite iocunda"; likely referring to the "good fight" of faith or the paradoxical joy of the Christian struggle</note>,
He had scattered these gifts in the former world with powerful fruit,
By which He taught the world, dedicating it, lest it prefer to go
Headlong here into worse places; the Master giving the laws
Of the Gospel to be known, and harsh customs to grow mild.
So that as God from the citadel of the pole and as the Just One, when the Author 
Shall have arrived there to give the rewards of the ethereal Father to the just,
His right hand may then take up good gifts for those with worthy merits.
Indeed, this number of the Healer <note>This likely refers to the symbolic number of letters or lines in the grid poem, which Hrabanus often used to encode theological meanings.</note> marks both
Advents of the Lord: when He drove away the tyrant <note>referring to the Devil or Satan</note> from here,
When, having been made man here, He returned such great goods to the world,
And after His baptism, He uttered proofs to all with His mouth.
This is when the Savior, coming from the Most High Father as the Just
Judge and as man—the trumpet <note>original: "sal pix", likely a corruption of the Greek "salpinx" (σάλπιγξ) meaning trumpet</note> carries him from here 
To give holy rewards on high, and to see even the sacred face
Of the One above: those whom true growth announces 
As having been produced by good merits to sing songs of praise:
Which the nourishing lot is wont to sing, as the serene writings 
Of the Apocalypse <note>The Book of Revelation</note> contain; there the clear hosts bring 
Glory and power; on every high day and throughout the ages,
Hallelujah <note>original: "Alleluia"</note> resounds. Oh, who would not wish to be in this hall!
And our God and Lord must be appeased everywhere,
So that this writing may help us, as the nourishing citadel of the air,
When He appears here, rejoicing for His servants, and the crowd 
Of the nourishing One snatches them up, losing nothing, and His wrath removes scandals,
So that He may send His devoted servants like wheat into the granary <note>A reference to the Gospel parable of the wheat and the tares (Matthew 13:30), where the wheat represents the saved.</note>.
Happy is he who is able and permitted to climb to heaven,
And to look well upon the joyful face of the Lord Christ:
For whom deep love remains, all perfection is returned,
And mixed with angelic choirs, he rejoices everywhere 
With praises, and strives to sing psalms to Christ:
Rightly singing new songs, he knows not how to set aside this devotion:
Because thus he then knows well the eternal kingdoms and joys.

<meta>This page provides the "Declaratio" (Explanation) for Figure XXII. It interprets the symbolic and numerical meaning of the Chi-Rho monogram (the Christogram) used in the previous visual grid, specifically linking the physical form of the letters to biblical prophecies from the Book of Daniel and the Book of Revelation.</meta>

-># EXPLANATION<-

What this figure is, then, and what it signifies, must be explained. This is one of those figures called "marks of meaning" <note>original: "notae sententiarum"; symbols used to convey complex theological ideas</note>, and by a special name the Greeks call it *chrisimon* <note>original: "chrifimon"; a Greek term for a symbol marking something as "useful" or "good," which Christians adopted as a monogram for Christ</note>, invented according to the will of each person to denote something. But it is adopted with greater dignity by Christians to express the name of Christ, as if the first two letters of His name were grasped together in one monogram: that is, **X** and **P** <note>The Greek letters Chi (X) and Rho (P), the first two letters of "Christos"</note>.

As for why it has been adopted by us in this work at this time, this is the reason: for in the figure itself is noted that number of days in which Christ is believed to have preached to the world, and that number which is to come before His second advent, from the times of the Antichrist until the end of the world, as explained by the orthodox teachers of the Church according to the prophecy of Daniel. Thus, in the letter **P**, the former number—that is, **1,260**—is found, which is three and a half years, the span of time in which Christ is known to have preached to the world. For the months of three and a half years—that is, forty-two months—make **1,260** days. Under this same number, the Holy City is described in the Apocalypse <note>The Book of Revelation</note> as being trodden underfoot by the nations, and the woman is described as fleeing from the face of the dragon into the wilderness, where she has a place prepared by God, so that she may be fed there for that same number of days. This number mystically encompasses all the times of Christianity, as the firm tradition of the Fathers holds. Because Christ, whose body this is, preached in the flesh for that length of time, the Church now either rejoices in the hope of eternal things during its pilgrimage in the present desert, or suffers the trouble of persecution from infidels or false brothers.

Therefore, the letter **X** contains that number which the prophecy of Daniel foretold would come in the time of the Antichrist: that is, **1,335** days. For it is written there: *Blessed is he who waits and reaches as far as 1,335 days.* Blessed Jerome explains this thus: "Blessed," he says, "is he who, after the Antichrist has been slain, waits forty-five days beyond the **1,290** days (that is, three and a half years), at which time the Lord and Savior is to come in His majesty." Why there is a silence of forty-five days after the killing of the Antichrist belongs to divine knowledge, unless perhaps we might say: the delay of the kingdom of the saints is a trial of patience.

But because the reason stated above is more manifest, if we write down the letters themselves which are inscribed in this figure and which form the monogram by their position, together with their number according to their order, let space be granted for the pen for this purpose. The letters placed in the **P** sound thus: **O SOTER IESOUS ALETHEIA** <note>original: "O. COTHP. IHCYC. AAHOIA"; Greek for "The Savior Jesus Truth"</note>, namely three names of Christ, which are interpreted in Latin as *Saving Savior, Truth*. 

But the two latter Greek names are written with their full sequence of letters: that is, **IESOUS** and **ALETHEIA**. The third, however, that is **SOTER**, according to the custom of Greek writing, is marked with three letters (excepting the article **O**): namely **S**, **E**, and **R** <note>original: "C. H. P."; using Latin characters to represent the Greek Sigma, Eta, and Rho</note>. And so all the letters written in the **P** become **15** in number. 

The first of these is **O**, marking the number **70**; the second is **S** <note>C</note>, signifying **200**; the third is **E** <note>H</note>, numbering **8**; the fourth is **R** <note>P</note>, expressing **100**; the fifth is **I**, **10**; the sixth is **E** <note>H</note>, **8**; the seventh is **S** <note>C</note>, **200**; the eighth is **U** <note>Y</note>, **400**; the ninth is **S** <note>C</note>, **200**; the tenth is **A**, **1**; the eleventh is **L** <note>Λ</note>, **30**; the twelfth is **E** <note>H</note>, **8**; the thirteenth is **TH** <note>Θ</note>, **9**; the fourteenth is **I**, **10**; the fifteenth is **A**, demonstrating **1**. 

When all these are joined together, they make the number **1,255**; and there still remain **5** to reach the aforementioned fullness of the number [1,260], which can still be found in the character of the **P** itself: that is, if the **P** itself is divided so that the uppermost part, which has the image of the letter **L** <note>Λ</note> in it, signifies the number four, and the lowest part, which forms a Latin **I**, shows the number one by the power of the Latins, and so... <note>The text cuts off mid-sentence, to be continued on the next page.</note>

the numbers one thousand, two hundred, and sixty are found in the letter **P** <note>The Greek letter Rho</note>. The letter **X** <note>The Greek letter Chi</note>, which is the other part of the monogram, similarly contains three names of the Lord, written in eight letters: that is, **GOD**, **CHRIST**, and **JESUS** <note>original Greek: THEOS, CHRESTOS, IESUS</note>. These are the letters and their values:

*   **Θ** <note>Theta</note> expressing 9
*   **C** <note>The "lunate sigma," equivalent to S</note> representing 200
*   **X** <note>Chi</note> representing 600
*   **P** <note>Rho</note> representing 100
*   **C** <note>Sigma</note> representing 200
*   **I** <note>Iota</note> representing 10
*   **H** <note>Eta</note> representing 8
*   **C** <note>Sigma</note> representing 200

Together, these make **1,327**. There remain **8** more, which are added if the letter **H** <note>Eta</note>—which is situated in the middle of the eight letters, acting as a nail <note>symbolizing the nails of the Crucifixion</note>—is added with the number eight from the letter **P**.

There are also three verses in the monogram, written with larger letters containing smaller ones inside. The first verse, beginning from **O**, goes around all the larger letters in a circuit; these form the shape of a **Δ** <note>The Greek letter Delta, often symbolizing the Trinity</note> at the top of the **P**, and they hold two Greek names: **THE SAVIOR JESUS** <note>original Greek: O SOTER IESUS</note>, comprised of nine letters. This verse reads: *For it is fitting that these nourishing writings shine from here in the name of Christ.*

The second verse is in the remaining part of the **P**—that is, in the vertical line that goes straight down—and it contains the name **TRUTH** <note>original Greek: ALETHEIA</note>, written in six Greek letters. It reads: **This holy, saving writing praises Christ.**

The third verse is in the letter **X**, containing the eight letters in which the three names—**GOD**, **CHRIST**, and **JESUS**—are noted. It reads: **Christ is man, and truly the gentle judge of this world as well.**

-># FIGURE XXIII.<-
->## Concerning the number twenty-four and its sacred mystery<-

<note>Hrabanus Maurus uses the number 24 (the product of 6 and 4) to symbolize the perfection of time—such as the 24 hours of the day—and the harmony of the physical world.</note>

Behold, the noble **flower** <note>Latin: *flos*; this word is highlighted in red in the original grid</note> shines, depicted in the King's name,
And these marks signify the deeds of the powerful victor.
The joyful horns of the cross are thus hidden in a **triple** <note>Latin: *trino*; highlighted in red</note> verse,
Which, with remarkable skill, count six units four times <note>6 multiplied by 4 equals 24.</note>,
And they **show** <note>Latin: *ostendunt*; highlighted in red</note> that perfect beauty exists in all things—
All things which the Almighty created and redeemed.
Bright is that day on which the Creator formed all things;
No less does this day shine on which the Teacher <note>Referring to Christ as the *Doctor* or Teacher of the world.</note> blessed all things.
Then the Creator, being good, fulfilled all good deeds;
Now the pious Lover has blessed all pious works.
Therefore, the sixfold world <note>Latin: *senarius orbis*. In medieval science, 6 was considered a "perfect number" because its factors (1, 2, and 3) add up to itself.</note> praises the four quarters of the earth.
The number six shines; it is the first perfect number and it is itself.
It divides the whole day, and it also binds it together;
It belongs to the year, the month, the leap year, and the quarter-day <note>Hrabanus is referencing how the number 6 is the basis for measuring time and astronomical cycles.</note>.
This counter is present, raising up the times at his nod,
He closes the ages without end and sets a limit for the world.
Then the Leader gives eternal life and shining kingdoms;
He grants the heavens to the pious, forgiving debts with his countenance.
From there, Jesus, marking us again, grants pious rewards in his favor
From all the world; to those whom such great flashing gifts
The living light of faith has led, and into whom it has poured its drafts.
True love adorns the just and blesses the nourishing work.
Therefore, marked by all the quarters of the world, yet here
The number is set down; behold, let the peoples from everywhere proceed
To the help of the cross, to ask for the pious divine power of Jesus.
And let them learn thoroughly the perfect beauty through perfect doctrine,
So that kind deeds may follow their perfect faith.
Indeed, all these things everywhere testify to the true God:
The perfect things, indeed, testify to the perfect and beautiful beauty,
Which the rotation of the pole adorns and which Heaven establishes,
Which the sea, the earth, and the hall of heaven contain.
But also we humans, a small portion in the order of things,
Let us rightly sound forth with song and voice the saving cross;
He who made us well, he who increased us, and he who redeemed us.
With song and in frequent celebration, let us sing of his loves,
Which he himself, by his sacred work and protection for us,
Has already expended; he urged, he commanded, he showed, he loved.

## FOLIO XLVII.

Behold, the noble **flower** <note>original: *flos*; this refers to a specific shape within the grid of the original poem</note> shines, depicted in the name of the King,
And with marks they signify the deeds of the powerful victor.
The joyful horns of the Cross are thus established in a **triple** <note>original: *trino*</note> verse,
Which count six <term>units<gloss>monades</gloss></term> four times with remarkable skill <note>6 multiplied by 4 equals 24, representing the 24 hours of the day and the 24 elders of the Apocalypse.</note>,
And they **show** <note>original: *ostendunt*</note> that perfect beauty exists in all things—
All things which the Almighty created and redeemed.
Bright is that day on which the Creator fashioned all things;
No less does this day shine on which the Teacher <note>Referring to Christ as the *Doctor* or instructor of humanity.</note> blessed all things.
Then the good Creator completed all good deeds;
Now the pious Lover <note>original: *amator*; a common medieval title for Christ as the lover of souls.</note> has blessed all pious works.
Therefore the <term>sixfold<gloss>senarius</gloss></term> world praises the four quarters of the earth:
The number six shines in its numbers; it is the first perfect number and it is itself <note>In medieval mathematics, 6 was "perfect" because its factors 1, 2, and 3 add up to 6.</note>.
It divides the whole day, and it also binds it together;
For the year, the month, the <term>leap year<gloss>bisextilis</gloss></term>, and the <term>quarter-day<gloss>quadrantis</gloss></term>,
This counter is present, lifting up the seasons at his nod.
He encompasses the ages at their end, and encloses the world within a boundary.
Then the Leader gives eternal life and bright kingdoms
Above the stars to the pious, forgiving debts; with his face
Jesus marks the bestowal of pious rewards; you know this,
Among all those in the world whom the flashing light of faith
Has led to such great gifts, and into whom he has poured living draughts.
True love decorates and blesses the nourishing work of the just;
Therefore, from all quarters of the world, this number placed here marks—
Behold!—the people proceeding from everywhere
To the help of the Cross, to pray to the pious divinity of Jesus;
And may they learn perfect beauty through perfect doctrine,
Because kind deeds follow perfect faith.
Truly all these things everywhere bear witness to the true God:
Perfect things to the Perfect One, beautiful things to the Beautiful One—
Those which the rotation of the pole turns, which <term>heaven<gloss>olympus</gloss></term> founds,
Which the sea, the earth, and the hall of heaven contain.
But we men also, a small portion in these things,
Let us duly sound the saving Cross with song and voice.
Let us sing of the one who made us well, who increased us, and who redeemed us,
And in celebrated song let us sing of his frequent loves,
Which he himself has already bestowed, urged, shown, ordered, and loved
For us through his sacred work and protection.

<meta>This page provides the prose explanation (Declaratio) for the preceding grid poem. It expands on the symbolic significance of the number twenty-four, linking the structure of the Cross to the rhythms of time, the books of the Bible, and the celestial hierarchy.</meta>

### EXPLANATION.

Behold, the <term>sixfold number<gloss>senarius</gloss></term> fittingly encompasses the four points of the Lord's Cross and displays the total perfection of the completed work. This is because upon the Cross, the Creator of all things delivered the judgment of His own fulfillment when, having received the cup, He said, *It is finished* <note>original: *consummatum est*; John 19:30</note>. For it is rightly written that all was "finished" at the moment the human race was set free; this act of Christ’s passion benefited not only humanity, who attained the grace of redemption, but also the celestial throngs of Angels, as they achieved the full completion of their own number through Him.

For four times six makes twenty-four, and by this number the circuit of the heavenly sphere revolves through its hours. By this same number, the course of the natural day is marked by the judgment of the circling stars. This is also the number of books of the Old Testament received into canonical authority among the Hebrews—counting **Ruth** and **Lamentations** <note>original: *Cynoth*, from the Hebrew *Qinoth*</note> as individual books—and it is the number into which the **Levitical tribe** was distributed into divisions by David, decreeing that all the sons of Aaron should serve God in turns. 

It is fitting, then, that the number of chosen high priests should foreshadow the eternal priesthood of Christ. Having become a high priest according to the **order of Melchizedek**, He offered Himself as an unblemished sacrificial victim to God upon the altar of the Cross—specifically, as that Lamb who took away the sins of the world. By the sprinkling of His blood, the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies were cleansed, and the filth of all sins was washed away through true atonement. 

The **elders** of this same number are described as sitting around that most powerful throne of which the **Apocalypse** <note>The Book of Revelation</note> speaks, from which proceed lightning, voices, and thunder. These elders designate the Church, brought forth through the two Testaments from the Patriarchs and the Apostles; because of its judicial dignity in Christ, the Church is seen sitting in a circle around that throne. Concerning this power, the Savior spoke when demonstrating the might of His kingdom: *And I, if I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all things to myself.* 

Indeed, the Savior drew all things to Himself when, placed upon the Cross, He subjected all power to Himself. Rising from this on the third day, He spoke to His disciples: *All power is given to me in heaven and on earth.* The Apostle also testified to this: *Christ became obedient for us to the Father even unto death, even the death of the Cross; because of which God also exalted him, and gave him a name which is above every name, so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of those in heaven, on earth, and under the earth, and every tongue should confess that the Lord Jesus is in the glory of God the Father.* 

Therefore, lightning, voices, and thunder proceed from this throne because, after the Savior's passion, resurrection, and ascension into heaven, His disciples (as Mark writes) went forth and preached everywhere, with God cooperating and confirming their word with following signs. One of them, when the Jews were gathered against him, answered with great authority: *Be it known to all of you and to all the people of Israel, that in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom you crucified, whom God raised from the dead, by him this man stands before you whole. This is the stone which was rejected by you builders, which has become the head of the corner; nor is there salvation in any other, for there is no other name under heaven given to men by which we must be saved.*

<meta>This page provides the theological "Declaration" or explanation for Figure 24. While the previous page presented the artistic and poetic arrangement of the 144,000 elect, this text explains the numerological symbolism and scriptural basis for the image, specifically drawing from the Book of Revelation and the Prophet Ezekiel.</meta>

-># EXPLANATION.<-
<meta>catchword: multi-</meta>

This figure of the Holy Cross, formed within four pentagons, contains a total of 144 letters arranged in four verses. According to the multiplication of this number by a thousand in the **Apocalypse** <note>The Book of Revelation (14:1–3)</note>, the multitude of those who were sealed from every tribe of the children of Israel is calculated. This signifies the number of those clothed in white who stood with the Lamb upon Mount **Sion** <note>Mount Zion, representing the heavenly Jerusalem</note>. In the thousands of the "sealed," we see the innumerable multitude of the entire Church, which is descended from the Patriarchs, whether by physical lineage or by the imitation of their faith. For as it is said: "If you are Christ's, then you are Abraham's seed" <note>Galatians 3:29</note>. To reach the height of perfection, the number twelve is multiplied by twelve <note>12 x 12 = 144</note>, and this sum is brought to completion by the thousand—which is the number ten made into a solid square <note>10 x 10 x 10 = 1,000. In medieval numerology, "solid" refers to a cubic number</note>—signifying the stable and eternal life of the Church.

From the moment the Lord suffered His passion, the power of worldly dominion was crushed. The empire of the nations was broken so that the faces of the saints could be freely marked with the sign of the faith they once resisted. The sign of faith is the Cross of Christ, in whose likeness the letter **Tau** <note>The Hebrew letter T, which in ancient scripts looked like a cross (+ or X)</note> is formed. Regarding this, it is written in **Ezekiel**: "And the glory of the God of Israel went up from the Cherub, which was under him, to the threshold of the house, and He called the man who was clothed in linen, who had a writer’s inkhorn at his side, and said to him: 'Go through the midst of the city, through the midst of **Jerusalem**, and mark a **Tau** upon the foreheads of the men who sigh and mourn over all the abominations that are committed in its midst.'" And he said to others in my hearing: "Go through the city after him and strike; let not your eye spare, nor have pity. Kill the old man, the young man, the virgin, the little child, and the women, even to utter destruction; but do not kill anyone upon whom you see the **Tau**," and so forth <note>Ezekiel 9:3–6</note>. Indeed, it is right that every wicked person is struck down by the blade of their own unbelief, for they are proven to have neglected showing the sign of faith through good works. Conversely, the righteous are justly delivered through the power of Christ's Cross by performing good works; for they are known to have kept the faith of the Lord—received in baptism—unviolated until the end by fulfilling Christ’s commandments.

Next, the flock of those made white is counted in that same numerical quantity, suggesting the vast number of the elect who have kept holy virginity. Yet, anyone of sound mind should understand that a finite number is used here to represent an infinite one. There is a hidden mystery in this measurement suited for those who live a virginal life: by loving God with all their heart, soul, and mind, their body—which consists of four elements—is also consecrated to Him in integrity. For three times three is nine, and four times four is sixteen; and sixteen times nine equals **144**. Thus, when such a perfect multitude is seen upon Mount Sion with the Lamb—composed of those who have chosen the narrower path of life—there can be no doubt regarding the other members of the Church. "And they sang as if a new song before the throne, and before the four living creatures and the elders," and so forth. They sing to God as if with their own lyre, those who, by the privilege of angelic chastity, make themselves a total <term>holocaust</term> <note>original: *holocaustũ*; here meaning a "whole burnt offering" or total sacrifice of the self</note> to the Lord. Taking up their cross, they follow the Lamb wherever He goes. They will sing "as if a new song" which no one else can sing: for to sing the song uniquely for the Lamb is to rejoice with Him forever, above all other faithful, specifically in the incorruption of the flesh. While the other elect can hear this song, they cannot speak it; through charity, they certainly rejoice in the high status of the virgins, even if they do not rise to the same rewards.

<margin>*</margin> The song of old was indeed: "Blessed is he who has seed in Sion, and servants in Jerusalem" <note>Isaiah 31:9</note>. And likewise: "Increase and multi-"

This refers to the Church of the Gentiles being more populous than the ancient Synagogue.</note>. And likewise the same Prophet says: *And let not the eunuch say, "Behold, I am a dry tree," for thus says the Lord to the eunuchs who have kept my sabbaths, and have chosen what I willed, and have held fast to my covenant: I will give to them in my house and within my walls a place, and a name better than sons and daughters; I will give them an everlasting name that shall not perish* <note>Isaiah 56:3–5</note>. Look: each of the four pentagons <term>pentagonus</term> <note>A five-sided geometric figure. Here, it refers to the shapes formed by letters in the accompanying diagram.</note> contains 36 letters. This is not simply because this number creates a five-angled figure—for 35 is actually a pentagonal number <note>In medieval arithmetic, 35 is the 5th pentagonal number; Maurus adds one to reach 36 for symbolic reasons.</note>—but it is positioned thus to suggest a certain mystery <term>sacramentum</term>. Therefore, the number five <term>quinarius</term> signifies the Law <note>The Pentateuch, or the five books of Moses.</note>, and the number four <term>quaternarius</term> signifies the Gospel. Now, the four pentagons, with the four units attached to them, complete the four "horns" <note>The four ends or arms of the Cross.</note>. This is because, once the passion and resurrection of Christ were completed, the Law and the Gospel together were committed to teachers to be preached throughout the whole breadth of the world. The fathers of both Testaments were given as an example, whom the faithful everywhere in the whole world strive to imitate by preserving chastity; joined to the Lamb upon Mount **Sion**, they sang as it were a new song upon their harps. 

Therefore, we have shown that the four units which cling to the pentagons on the outside form one name in four letters—that is, **CRUX** <note>Latin for "Cross."</note>—so that they might cling to their pentagons to complete the verses, and be woven together by that one name to demonstrate their shared purpose. There is also a verse in the higher part of the Cross: **The immaculate cohort, you sing there with your voices.** And in the bottom part, this one: **Where King Jesus triumphs, where the Lamb of the Virgin feeds.** On the right side indeed is this: **Songs which no one sings with a widespread speech.** And on the left is this: **Here is your flock alone and a splendid order.**

# EXPLANATION

-> 11 <-

Therefore, this figure of the Holy Cross, formed within four pentagons, contains the number 144 [CXLIV] in its letters, written in four verses. According to the plurality of this number—which is multiplied by a thousand in the Apocalypse <note>original: "in Apocalypsi"; referring to the Book of Revelation 7:4 and 14:1-3</note>—that multitude of the sealed is calculated from every tribe of the sons of Israel. This denotes the number of those clothed in white who stood with the Lamb upon Mount Sion. First, in the thousands of those who are sealed, an innumerable multitude of the entire Church is signified, which is descended from the Patriarchs, whether by physical lineage or by the imitation of faith. For as it is said, *If you are Christ’s, then you are Abraham’s seed* <note>Galatians 3:29</note>. Furthermore, to increase this sense of perfection, the number twelve [XII] is itself multiplied by twelve, and this sum is perfected by a thousand—which is the number ten made into a solid square <note>10 x 10 x 10 = 1000. In medieval numerology, the cube (solid square) represented stability and eternity.</note>—signifying the stable and eternal life of the Church.

From the moment the Lord suffered, the empire of worldly rule was crushed, and the power of the nations was broken to this end: so that the faces of the saints might be freely marked with the sign of faith which they once resisted.

The sign of faith is the Cross of Christ, in whose likeness the letter **Tau** is formed <term>Tau</term> <note>The last letter of the Hebrew alphabet. In ancient script, it was written as a cross-like mark (+ or X), which early Christians interpreted as a prophecy of the Crucifixion.</note>. Regarding this, it is written in Ezekiel:
> And the glory of the Lord of Israel was taken up from the Cherub, which was under Him, to the threshold of the house; and He called to the man who was clothed in linen and had a writer's inkhorn at his loins, and said to him: "Go through the midst of the city, through the midst of Jerusalem, and mark a **Tau** upon the foreheads of the men who sigh and mourn over all the abominations that are committed in its midst." Kill the old men, the young men and maidens, the little ones and the women, even to utter destruction; but do not kill any man upon whom you see the **Tau**," and so forth. <note>Ezekiel 9:3–6</note>

Rightly is every wicked person slain by the blade of infidelity, for they are proven to have neglected to show the sign of faith through good works within themselves. Justly, then, is every good person who performs good works liberated through the power of the Cross of Christ: because they are recognized as having kept the faith of the Lord (which they received at baptism) inviolate until the end by fulfilling the commandments of Christ.

Next, that white-clad flock is counted in the quantity of that same number [144], and the abundant number of those in holy virginity among the elect is made known. However, anyone who is wise in spirit ought to understand that a finite number is used here to represent an infinite one. By the meaning of a hidden mystery, this number is suitable for examining the company of virgins: for one who loves God with all their heart, all their soul, and all their mind, is also consecrated to Him in the integrity of the body (which consists of four elements). For three times three [3x3] are nine [IX], and four times four [4x4] are sixteen [XVI]; sixteen times nine [16x9] fulfills the number 144 [CXLIV]. Thus, when this most perfect multitude—consisting of those established in the degree of the stricter life—is seen with the Lamb on Mount Sion, there is no doubt concerning the other members of the Church.
> And they sang, as it were, a new song before the throne, and before the four living creatures and the elders, and so forth. <note>Revelation 14:3</note>

They sing to God as if with their own lyre, those who, through the privilege of angelic chastity, make themselves a total burnt offering <note>original: "holocaustum"</note> to the Lord. ### DECLARATION.

Therefore, this figure of the holy Cross, formed within four pentagons, contains the number of 144 [cxliv] letters, written in four verses. According to its plural nature, when multiplied by a thousand, it represents that multitude of the sealed in the **Book of Revelation** <note>original: "Apocalypsi"</note>, calculated from every tribe of the children of Israel. It denotes that number of those clothed in white who stood with the Lamb upon Mount Sion. First, in the thousands of the sealed, the countless multitude of the entire Church is signified—those descended from the Patriarchs, whether by physical lineage or by the imitation of faith. For, as it is said, "If you are Christ’s, then you are Abraham’s seed" <note>Galatians 3:29</note>. 

Furthermore, the multiplication of twelve [xii] by twelve pertains to the increase of perfection, reaching its final sum in the thousand, which is a solid square of the number ten [denarius] <note>In medieval mathematics, a "solid" number often refers to a cube; 10 x 10 x 10 equals 1,000, representing three-dimensional stability and spiritual completion.</note>, signifying the stable life of the Church. From the moment the Lord suffered, the empire of worldly rule was crushed, and the power of the nations was broken, so that the faces of the saints—which had once been resisted—might be freely marked with the sign of faith. 

The sign of faith is, therefore, the Cross of Christ, in whose likeness the letter **Tau** <note>The Hebrew letter Tau was traditionally written as a cross-like mark (+) or a T-shape, making it a common Christian symbol for the Cross of Christ.</note> is formed. Regarding this, it is written in **Ezekiel**: *And the glory of the Lord of Israel was taken up from the Cherub, which was under him, to the threshold of the house; and he called the man who was clothed in linen, and had a writer’s inkhorn at his loins, and said to him: "Go through the midst of the city, through the midst of Jerusalem, and mark a **Tau** upon the foreheads of the men who groan and mourn over all the abominations that are committed in its midst."* And he said to the others in my hearing: *"Go through the city following him and strike; let your eye not spare, nor have any pity. Kill the old man, the youth, and the maiden, the infant, and the women, until they are utterly destroyed; but do not kill anyone upon whom you see the **Tau**,"* and so forth <note>Ezekiel 9:3–6</note>. 

Rightly is every wicked person slain by the blade of infidelity, for they are proven to have neglected to show the sign of faith through good works within themselves. Justly, any of the good is liberated by performing good works through the power of Christ’s Cross, because he is recognized to have kept the faith of the Lord—which he received in baptism—inviolate until the end by fulfilling the commandments of Christ.

Next, that flock of those "made white" is counted in the quantity of that same number, and the abundant multitude of holy virginity among the chosen is made known. However, any person of sound mind should understand that a finite number is used here to represent an infinite one. By the significance of a secret mystery, it is suited to the examination of virgins: one who loves God with all their heart, soul, and mind, is also consecrated to Him in the integrity of the body (which consists of four [iv] elements). For three times three is nine [ix], and four times four is sixteen [xvi], but sixteen times nine completes the 144 [cxliv]. Thus, while this perfect multitude is seen upon Mount Sion with the Lamb—consisting of those established in the rank of a "stricter life" <term>arctioris vitæ; refers to the disciplined life of monastics or ascetics</term>—there should be no doubt regarding the other members of the Church. 

*And they sang, as it were, a new song before the throne, and before the four living creatures and the elders,* and so forth <note>Revelation 14:3</note>. Those who, by the privilege of angelic chastity, make themselves a "whole burnt offering" <term>holocaustum; a sacrifice entirely consumed by fire, symbolizing total devotion</term> to the Lord, sing to God as if with their own lyre. Taking up their cross, they follow the Lamb wherever He goes, and they shall sing, as it were, a new song which no one else can sing. For to sing a song uniquely to the Lamb is to rejoice with Him forever above all other faithful, specifically regarding the incorruptibility of the flesh. Yet, the other chosen ones can hear the song, even if they cannot speak it; for through charity, they are indeed joyful in the high standing of those others, even if they do not rise to their specific rewards. 

The old song was: *Blessed is he who has seed in Sion, and a household in Jerusalem* <note>Isaiah 31:9</note>. And likewise: *Increase and...*

"be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth." <note>Genesis 1:28</note> For it is a new thing: "Rejoice, O barren one who does not bear; break forth and cry out, you who do not travail, for many more are the children of the desolate than of her who has a husband." <note>Isaiah 54:1; Galatians 4:27</note> And likewise the same Prophet says: "And let not the eunuch say, 'Behold, I am a dry tree.' For thus says the Lord to the eunuchs who have kept my sabbaths, and have chosen what I willed, and have held fast to my covenant: I will give to them in my house and within my walls a place, and a name better than sons and daughters; I will give them an everlasting name that shall not perish." <note>Isaiah 56:3-5</note> And again: "Blessed are the barren who have not given birth, and the breasts that have not nursed," and so forth. <note>Luke 23:29</note> Indeed, they have his name and the name of his father written on their foreheads: because the Church, dedicated in the confession of the Holy Trinity, carries the sign of her faith on her forehead, which is painted through the mystery of the Holy Cross on the foreheads of Christians, and is signed by the frequent tracing of the hand <note>original: "manus inscriptione"; referring to the practice of making the sign of the cross</note>. 

Behold, each of the four [iv] pentagons contains thirty-six [xxxvi] letters: but not because this number itself makes the shape of five angles. For thirty-five [xxxv] is a pentagonal number <note>In medieval mathematics, a "pentagonal number" is a figurate number; 35 is the 5th pentagonal number (1, 5, 12, 22, 35). Hrabanus notes he has added one letter to each for symbolic reasons.</note>: but it is positioned thus to intimate some sacred mystery <note>original: "sacramentum"</note>. The number five [quinarius], therefore, signifies the Law <note>The Pentateuch, or first five books of the Bible</note>, and the number four [quaternarius] signifies the Gospel: but the four pentagons, with the four units <note>single letters</note> clinging to them, complete the four [iv] horns <note>The "horns" or points of the cross</note>. Because the Law and the Gospel, completed by the passion and resurrection of Christ, were entrusted to teachers to be preached across the entire breadth of the world: following the example given by the fathers of both testaments, the faithful everywhere in the whole world strive to imitate them by preserving chastity; they, joined with the Lamb upon Mount Sion, sang as it were a new song upon their harps. 

Therefore, we have shown that the four units which cling to the outside of the pentagons form one name in four letters—that is, **CRUX** <note>Latin for "Cross"</note>—so that they might both cohere with their pentagons to complete the verses, and be joined to one another by a single name to demonstrate their rightful place. There is also this verse in the more eminent <note>top</note> part of the Cross: **O immaculate cohort, you sing there with your voices.** And in the bottom part, this: **Where King Jesus triumphs, where the Lamb of the Virgin grazes.** On the right side indeed is this: **Songs which no one else sings with such far-reaching speech.** And on the left is this: **Here is your flock, if not alone, then a splendid order.**

# DECLARATION.

Therefore, this figure of the holy Cross, formed in four pentagons, contains the number **144** [cxliv] in letters, written in four verses. According to the abundance of this number multiplied by a thousand, that multitude of the sealed is calculated from every tribe of the sons of Israel in the Apocalypse <note>The Book of Revelation</note>; and that number of those dressed in white, who stood with the Lamb upon Mount Sion, is denoted. First, in the thousands of the sealed, the innumerable multitude of the entire Church is signified, which is brought forth from the Patriarchs, either by physical lineage or by the imitation of faith. For if, he says, you are Christ's, then you are the seed of Abraham. Moreover, it pertains to the increase of perfection that the number **12** [xii] itself is multiplied twelve times, and perfected to its sum by a thousand, which is a solid square number <note>original: "denarius numerus quadratus solidus"; referring to 10x10x10, or 1,000, signifying three-dimensional stability and completion</note> of ten, signifying the stable life of the Church. Therefore, from the moment the Lord suffered, the empire of worldly rule was crushed, and the power of the nations was broken to this end: so that by the sign of faith which they had resisted, the faces of the saints might be freely marked. The sign of faith is thus the Cross of Christ, in whose likeness the letter **Tau** was formed <note>The Hebrew letter Tau (T) was historically written as a cross-like mark; it was seen by medieval scholars as a prophetic symbol of the Cross of Christ</note>, concerning which it is written in Ezekiel:

For every wicked person is rightly slain by the blade of infidelity, who is proved to have neglected to show the sign of faith through good work in himself; and deservedly, each of the good is liberated through the power of Christ's Cross by performing a good work: because he is recognized to have kept the faith of the Lord, which he received in baptism, inviolate until the end by fulfilling the commandments of Christ. Thus, when a multitude so perfect is seen upon Mount Sion with the Lamb, consisting of those who were established in the higher rank of the stricter life, there can be no doubt concerning the other members of the Church. <note>This grid of letters is a "poem within a poem." The bolded letters in the original Latin form internal words that create the shape of the cross. Vertically, they spell **CRUX** (Cross) and **LAUS** (Praise). Horizontally and diagonally, they spell **AMEN** and **ALLELUIA**. This visual technique reinforces the idea that the Cross is the structure upon which all sacred speech rests.</note>

Pious, perpetual praise of the saints in the light above
Assists those born of earth, so that they might worthily speak.
Now they may be strong concerning you, and eagerly fulfill what is fitting,
That mouths might be able to use good measures <note>original: "modulis"</note> and nourishing songs.
For indeed I have sung of you, I stand at the **Cross** in a living poem,
Wishing in verses to sing and to render my vows.
But you, surpassing all our poor gifts,
Powerful in majesty, you conquer earthly things—you conquer
The high stars of the pole; nor is any honor sufficient.
For to make things worthy of yours, or even to add words,
I have tried; therefore here, I pray <note>The Latin "voro" is likely a poetic variation of "oro," to pray, or perhaps "voveo," to vow.</note> for mystical things from the skies,
To bring words to you, contemplating the fitting figure.
I have arranged the song in signs and in a scattered path;
I have woven in angelic sounds with fitting verses.
Truly **Amen** in the middle pledges the seals <note>original: "signacula"</note> of life;
**Alleluia** completes the figure, surrounding the horns <note>The "horns" of the cross refer to the ends of the horizontal and vertical beams.</note> of the cross,
And marks the sacred image with a heavenly poem.
For the just from here receive scepters devoutly and all their rewards;
They surpass [the world], telling now of the glow of hope.
Sent down, may it give the prizes of the palm, and once the "bite" is removed <note>A reference to the "bite" of the forbidden fruit in Eden, which brought death to humanity.</note>
May that envious stock flee, which harmed the first race
Of the human kind; it fiercely swallowed them up and
The whole offspring, and dragged them into the depths of the abyss.
But us, as many as love has raised to the heavens from here,
Duly let us please the sacred face of the Lord with a poem—
With that poem which shall be in the high seats [of heaven],
Which the singing just shall sing with perpetual vow.
And this then duly pleases, if we fulfill the commands of the Thunderer <note>original: "tonantis" — a poetic title for God, originally used for Jupiter, signifying His power over the heavens.</note>
With our minds and our appearance, by our deeds and the speech of our tongue.
For speech alone is not the dear reward the just
Will receive; rather, it is true virtue with good hope.
For this praise is not good praise, but a false pretense,
If it sings great things and desires high things, but deserves only small ones.
Therefore come, you people, praise Christ faithfully with odes—
Heavenly populations, you Virtues <note>One of the nine choirs of angels.</note> and you powerful ones,
And the throngs of the just who stand in the citadel of heaven:
Sing "Amen, Alleluia" through the ages to Christ!

<summary>In this figure poem, Hrabanus Maurus weaves the liturgical shouts of "Alleluia" and "Amen" into a visual cross, calling upon both angels and humans to unite in sincere praise of Christ. The text emphasizes that true worship must be reflected in virtuous living, not just in beautiful words or songs.</summary>

# BOOK ONE. FOLIO LL.

Pious and perpetual praise of the saints in heavenly light,
stand by those born of earth, so they may be worthy to say
something of you now, and may decently fill their eager mouths
with good rhythms and nourishing songs.
Indeed, I have sung of you, O Cross, in this living poem,
in verses, desiring to return my vows through singing.
But you, O Cross, excelling all our gifts,
mighty in majesty, you surpass all earthly things; you surpass
the high stars of the sky, nor is anyone strong enough
to perform honors worthy of you, nor to add sufficient words.
And so, I have attempted here to draw mystical words from the heavens
for you by my vow, contemplating what is fitting for the figure.
I have arranged it with signs, and along a scattered path
I have inserted angelic songs, and woven them into fitting verses.
Truly, "Amen" <note>original: "amen"; a Hebrew word signifying "so be it," used here as a liturgical seal of truth</note> in the middle promises the seals of life;
"Alleluia" <note>original: "alleluia"; a call to "Praise Yahweh," representing the highest form of liturgical joy</note> completes it, surrounding the arms <note>original: "cornua"; literally "horns," referring to the four points or extremities of the cross</note> of the cross,
and marks the sacred image with a heavenly song.
For from here, the just ones devoutly [receive] their scepters and all gifts;
they surpass [others] by telling now how the fire of hope,
breathed into the mouth, gives the rewards of the palm <note>a symbol of victory and martyrdom</note>, and let that distant death
flee away—that envious death which harmed the first branch
of the human race, and fiercely swallowed up
the whole offspring and dragged them into the lowest depths.
But as many of us as love lifts to the heavens from here,
let us rightly please the sacred face of the Lord with song;
for with that song, which will be in the high dwellings,
which the just sing and will sing with perpetual vow,
this then rightly pleases Him, if we fulfill the commands of the Thunderer <note>original: "tonantis"; a classical epithet for a supreme deity (Jupiter), here adapted to refer to the power of the Christian God</note>
in our minds, in our forms, in our deeds, and in the speech of our tongues.
For such speech will not only receive the dear rewards of the just,
but true virtue will receive Him through well-spoken words.
This praise is not good praise, but a false fiction of the truth,
if it sings of great things and desires high things, but deserves only small ones.
Therefore, come, you heavenly people, you virtues, and you powerful
ranks of the just who stand in the citadel of heaven,
faithfully praise Christ with songs;
sing "Amen, Alleluia" through the ages to Christ.

### Figure XXV. Concerning the Alleluia and Amen, arranged in the form of a cross.

Pious and eternal praise of the saints in the light above,
assist those born of earth with something they may be worthy to speak,
that they may now be able to fill their eager mouths appropriately
concerning you with good measures and nourishing songs.
Indeed, I have sung of you, O Cross, in this living poem,
desiring in my verses to offer up my vows in song.
But you, surpassing all our gifts,
mighty in majesty, you overcome all earthly things; you overcome
the high stars of the sky, nor is any honor sufficient
for your sacred dignity, nor any words enough to add.
And so, I have attempted here to draw mystical words from the heavens
for you, contemplating a fitting arrangement for the figure.
I have disposed the signs along a scattered path of song,
I have inserted angelic [words] and woven them into fitting verses.
Truly, "Amen" <note>original: "amen"; a Hebrew term meaning "truly" or "so be it," used to seal a prayer or statement of faith</note> in the middle promises the seals of life;
"Alleluia" <note>original: "alleluia"; a Hebrew expression meaning "praise the Lord," representing the highest form of liturgical joy</note> completes it, surrounding the arms <note>original: "cornua"; literally "horns," signifying the four points or extremities of the cross</note> of the cross,
and marks the sacred image with a heavenly song.
For from here the just, with devotion, [receive] their scepters and all gifts;
now the fire of hope surpasses [all things] as they speak.
May the breath [of God] grant the rewards of the palm <note>a traditional symbol of victory and martyrdom</note>, and may that distant death
flee away—the envious death which harmed the first branch <note>original: "stirpem"; referring to Adam and the origins of humanity</note>
of the human race, and fiercely swallowed up
the whole offspring and dragged them into the depths of the abyss.
But as many of us as Love has raised from here into the heavens,
let us rightly please the sacred countenance of the Lord with song;
for by that song which shall be in the high dwellings,
which the just sing, they shall sing with a perpetual vow.
And this then rightly pleases, if I fulfill the commands of the Thunderer <note>original: "tonantis"; a poetic epithet for God, highlighting His divine power and authority</note>
with our minds, and with the appearance of our deeds, and with the thread of our tongue.
For words alone do not receive these dear rewards of the just,
but true virtue well-woven <note>original: "persamina"; referring to the thoroughness or "sifting" of one's character and actions</note> with them.
Since this praise is not good praise, but a false fiction of truth,
if she who sings of great and high things deserves only small things.
Therefore, come, you heavenly peoples, praise the writing faithfully with songs,
you Virtues <note>one of the nine traditional choirs of angels</note> and you Powers <note>another choir of angels</note>,
and the multitudes of the just who stand in the citadel of heaven,
sing "Amen, Alleluia" through the ages to Christ.

<summary>In this poem, Rabanus Maurus visually encodes the liturgical chants "Amen" and "Alleluia" into the shape of the cross, arguing that true praise must combine vocal beauty with virtuous living. The text calls upon both humans and the angelic hierarchies to join in a perpetual song of worship to Christ.</summary>

# FOLIO 51.

## BOOK ONE.

Pious and eternal praise of the saints in the heavenly light, assist those born of earth, so that they may now be worthy to say something of you, and may be able to fill their eager mouths appropriately with good rhythms and nourishing songs. Indeed, I have sung of you, O **Cross** <note>original: "Crux"</note>, in this living poem, desiring through singing also to fulfill my vows in these verses. 

But you, excelling above all our gifts, powerful in your majesty, you conquer earthly things; you conquer the high stars of the sky. Nor is any person strong enough to perform deeds worthy of your honor, nor to add sufficient words. Therefore, I have attempted here, by a vow, to draw mystical words from the heavens for you, contemplating what is fitting for the figure <note>Refers to the "carmina figurata" or pattern poem, where the letters are arranged in a grid to form a picture.</note>. I have arranged it with signs, and within a scattered path I have inserted angelic songs and woven them into fitting verses.

Truly, **Amen** <note>original: "amen"; a Hebrew term of affirmation</note> in the middle promises the seals <note>original: "signacula"; refers to the spiritual sealing of the believer</note> of life; **Alleluia** <note>original: "Alleluia"; Hebrew for "Praise the Lord"</note> completes the figure, surrounding the horns <note>original: "cornua"; a term for the four points or arms of the cross</note> of the cross, and marks the sacred image with a heavenly song. For from here the just, with devotion, receive scepters and all gifts; they excel, narrating now how the heat of hope, sent into the mouth, gives the rewards of the palm <note>A traditional symbol of victory and martyrdom.</note>, and how that far-off death flees away—that envious death which harmed the first stock of mankind <note>Refers to Adam and the Fall.</note> and, ferocious, swallowed the whole human race and dragged the entire offspring into the depths of the abyss. 

But as many of us as love lifts up to the heavens from here, let us duly please the sacred face of the Lord with song. For with that song which will be in the high dwellings, which the just sing and will sing with perpetual vow, this then pleases Him rightly, if we fulfill the commands of the **Thunderer** <note>original: "tonantis"; a classical poetic epithet for God, used here to describe the Christian God as the ruler of the heavens.</note> with our minds, and our appearance, our deeds, and the speech of our tongue. 

For speech alone will not receive these dear rewards of the just, but true virtue will, through well-spoken words. This praise would not be good praise, but a false fiction of the truth, if it were to sing great things and desire high things, yet deserve little by its actions. Therefore, come! Praise Christ faithfully with odes, you heavenly peoples, you powers, and you mighty ranks of the just who stand in the citadel of heaven: sing **Amen**, **Alleluia**, through the ages to Christ.

# EXPLANATION.

<unclear>p. 11. O.</unclear>
<meta>catchword: Worthy</meta>

There therefore that praise, which the voice of the saints in heaven is believed to
continually sing to God, imitates the shape of the holy Cross in writing—namely,
"Alleluia" <note>original: "alleluia"; a Hebrew expression meaning "Praise the Lord"</note> and "Amen" <note>original: "amen"; a Hebrew expression meaning "Truly" or "So be it"</note>—which John the Apostle and Evangelist writes in the Apocalypse <note>The Book of Revelation</note>. He writes that after the killing and drowning of the great harlot <note>The "Whore of Babylon," representing corrupt worldly power</note>, who seduced all nations in her fornication and with whom the kings of the earth committed fornication, he heard the voice of many crowds devoutly singing in heaven and repeating it often. For so it is written there: *After these things I heard as it were the voice of much people in heaven, saying: Alleluia, salvation, and glory, and power is to our God, for true and righteous are his judgments, because he has judged the great harlot, who corrupted the earth with her prostitution, and he has avenged the blood of his servants at her hands. And again they said: Alleluia. And her smoke rose up for ever and ever. And the twenty-four elders and the four animals fell down and adored God who sat upon the throne, saying: Amen, Alleluia. And a voice came out from the throne, saying: Give praise to our God, all you his servants, and you that fear him, little and great. And I heard as it were the voice of a great crowd, and as the voice of many waters, and as the voice of great thunderings, saying: Alleluia, for the Lord our God almighty has reigned. Let us be glad and rejoice and give glory to his name, for the marriage of the Lamb has come, and his wife has prepared herself. And it was granted to her that she should clothe herself in fine linen, glittering and white; for the fine linen is the righteous deeds of the saints,* and so forth. For although all these things were foretold concerning the future joy of the saints in heaven after the resurrection, nevertheless the Church sings them even now in part, having been made safe in hope; but then she shall sing them perfectly, when the separation has been made and when she is more clearly vindicated. After the universal judgment of the Lord, therefore, they shall be separated entirely from the goats <note>A reference to the biblical parable of the sheep and the goats (Matthew 25)</note>, and the wicked shall go into eternal punishment, but the just into eternal life. Now indeed the souls of the saints go into paradise after death, and those of the wicked into punishment, as the Lord demonstrated in the case of the poor man and the rich man <note>The parable of Lazarus and Dives (Luke 16)</note>; but their bodies await the end of the world. Now single white robes <note>original: "stolae"</note> are given to the just when they receive eternal rest in their souls; but then double robes shall be given, when their bodies, having been granted immortality, shall receive the everlasting kingdom together with their souls. The marriage of the Lamb will then truly appear when the whole Church is joined to the Lord in the chamber of the heavenly kingdom; and then this song will be perfectly frequented, when the joy of the whole Church shall be made perfect. Therefore, although these two Hebrew words, that is, "Alleluia" and "Amen," can be translated—for "Alleluia" is interpreted as "Praise the Lord," and "Amen" is translated as "In faith" or "In truth"—nevertheless, out of reverence for the holiness of that first language, their authority is preserved. And the Church sings "Alleluia" continually on Sundays and throughout the entire fifty-day season <note>original: "quinquagesimae"; the season of Pentecost or Eastertide</note>, because of the hope of resurrection which is found in the future praise of the Lord. But "Amen" is responded by the devotion of the faithful at the priest’s prayer or blessing in order to obtain that same perpetual life—indeed, every good thing that one hopes to receive from the Lord in the present or in the future. The arrangement of these words, therefore, fits the holy Cross aptly: because through the Cross itself the confession of all things has been united in the praise of the Lord, the number of angels is filled, the heavenly army is increased, the people of the saints are gathered, entrance to eternal life is granted to them, and the ancient curse is dissolved because a new blessing is established. Wherefore, in the aforementioned book, the twenty-four elders and the four animals sang a new song to the Lamb, saying:

<summary>Hrabanus Maurus explains the theological significance of placing the words "Alleluia" and "Amen" in the shape of a cross, drawing parallels between the liturgy and the celestial worship described in the Book of Revelation.</summary>

### Figure XXVI. On the sayings of the Prophets, which pertain to the passion of Christ and to our redemption.

<note>This poem is a "carmina figurata" (shaped poem). The text is arranged in a grid where the 18th horizontal line and the 19th vertical column form a cross. The letters within the cross shape create distinct sentences that can be read both across and down.</note>

Therefore, O Cross, the speech of the prophets honors you well,
It proclaims, exalts, and thunders your future deeds;
What the people, inspired by the sacred mouth, then brought forth,
And what the Holy Spirit had commanded them from within.
When they all speak of Christ restoring the world, and how, in you,
The Lord, fixed [to the wood], grants kingdoms to the kind.
**David** <note>King David, traditionally regarded as the author of the Psalms</note> spoke of his pierced palms and feet here,
And said that gall would be given for food, and vinegar for a drink;
And from your wood, he brings the King himself to all.
**Isaiah** <note>The "Evangelical Prophet" who foretold the Suffering Servant</note> prays that the empire be upon the shoulders of this boy,
With a blessed mouth, he spoke of the struck body and the hands extended,
Considering the spat-upon face, the death, and the cunning [of enemies],
And that the dispersed of Israel run to you, who are raised up.
**Jeremiah** <note>The weeping prophet who foretold the New Covenant</note> describes the lamb as if a burnt offering,
The pious one drawn without a voice, to be fed on wood. <note>original: "lignoque cibandum"; a reference to Jeremiah 11:19, often interpreted by Church Fathers as the Cross being "wood in his bread."</note>
**Ezekiel** sees in a vision the sign of the letter *Tau*, <note>original: "tau grammate"; the Hebrew letter Tau (X or T shape) was seen as a prefiguration of the Cross in Ezekiel 9:4.</note>
To rescue the people, in the likeness of the leading cross.
->You are pleasing to those above, O Cross; you are the pilot for this world.<-
<note>The line above forms the horizontal beam of the cross in the original grid.</note>
For **Daniel** <note>The prophet who predicted the timing of the Messiah's coming</note> said that Christ here, by the wicked people,
Would be punished, and then all harmful things would reach their end.
**Hosea** proclaims the people to be saved by the death of death itself,
And **Joel** had foretold in that hour
That neither sun nor stars would pour light upon the lands.
**Amos** had foretold this same thing and the ill-omened feasts.
**Obadiah** [fashioned] the snares, and **Jonah** the death [and burial].
**Micah** [proclaims] from the mountain; **Nahum** announces what the vengeance is.
**Habakkuk** proclaims with his mouth the holy horns of the cross. <note>Habakkuk 3:4 describes "horns" or "rays" coming from God's hands, often linked to the nails of the Cross.</note>
And **Zephaniah** long ago heard the bitter day of the Lord.
**Haggai** said the heavens and the earth would be moved.
**Zechariah** marks Jesus again through the filthy garments, <note>Zechariah 3:3; a vision of the High Priest Joshua (Jesus) in filthy rags, symbolizing taking on human sin.</note>
And says many will wail for the wounds fixed in his hands.
**Malachi** <note>The final prophet of the Old Testament</note> sees the Highest ruling through the world,
And the world in a burning fire and the ministers poured out.
The righteous elders of old spoke of these your deeds with their mouths;
O nourishing Cross, the Author brought forth these prophets, and in these,
You, O pious Passion of Christ, have fulfilled all these things.

<summary>This page contains a grid poem where the names and specific prophecies of sixteen Old Testament prophets are woven together to show how the Passion of Christ and the Cross were divinely preordained. The central cross-shaped text identifies the Cross as the "pilot" or "navigator" for the world.</summary>

<meta>This page follows the introduction to Figure XXVI, continuing the catalog of Old Testament prophets whose writings were interpreted by medieval scholars as prefigurations of Christ’s crucifixion and the power of the Cross.
