<header>BOOK TWO</header>

...you had previously pronounced. And what of you, O Raphael, the "Medicine of God"? <note>The name Raphael translates from Hebrew as "God heals."</note> Did you not, in that mystical work where you opened the eyes of Tobias by smearing his pupils with gall, signify the power of the Holy Cross? Through the bitterness of Christ’s death, the darkness of sins was removed, and eternal light was restored to the human race. We must believe, therefore, that the deeds of the Angels recorded in the Old Testament foreshadow the coming and glory of our Redeemer; just as the New Testament describes how, at the very beginning of his birth, they sang "Glory in the highest" with great joy and dancing, and wished peace upon men. Therefore, we also humbly beseech you, O noble armies of Angels: offer unceasing and worthy thanks to our Savior, and bless His holy name forever. He has freed us from perpetual death through the Cross and has filled your number—lest it remain diminished because of the lost angels <note>A common medieval belief that humans were created to replace the fallen angels who followed Lucifer.</note>—with holy souls in the celestial citadel.

### *On the form of the fourth figure, where Cherubim and Seraphim are depicted next to the Cross.*

<margin>4</margin> But you, O heavenly cohorts of Cherubim and Seraphim, now praise from heaven the name of your King, Jesus Christ. For the fire of your love and wisdom burns so well when it shines in the pure speech of the Redeemer's praise. That praise is true and divine when our Passover <note>original: "Pascha nostrum"</note>—which is the passion and resurrection of our Redeemer—is truly proclaimed to be our life. Truly, the fruit of light is Christ, whom you celebrate with shared praise as the Lord God of Hosts <note>original: "Dominum Deum Sabaoth"</note> along with the Father and the Holy Spirit. He, in the hour of his passion, conquered the sorrow of death, and now reigning everywhere, he exults in the joy of the resurrection. O blessed Seraphim, tell us of the heat of your love; show us if your celestial laws are made manifest in this celebration; if you signify by this many-voiced and powerful praise, reveal the heavenly Victor.

Hence, I confidently answer for you, for myself, and for my people in this way. For there is one thing they show us, which they affirm in the positioning of their wings: that the altar of the Holy Cross was long ago foretold to us in symbolic figures, as was the sacred beauty of the Victim who was sacrificed upon it. They also utter Christ's vows of praise—the power of our redemption and the goodness of the rewards which King Christ decreed to grant us. When he suffered on this altar according to his fruitful purpose, he consumed the iniquities and sins of our crimes in the flame of his passion. Overcoming all opposing powers at the moment of his death, he conquered them; and casting out the prince of this world <note>A reference to the Devil.</note>, he broke apart his destroyed prisons. Our kind Lord and King of Virtues wiped away the old age of our sins, restoring to us the very kingdoms of Paradise in which the first man had been created and placed.

The mouths of all the faithful prove this: and the virtues and miracles which God performs in this world through his saints testify that God gave the help of his commandments to the human race—rightly condemned to the prison and darkness of this world—for the sake of escaping perpetual death. Our Creator and King was fixed for us upon the high beam of the cross; it is more fitting to call this an imperial throne than a slave’s torture <note>The cross was a punishment for the lowest classes in Rome, but is here re-imagined as a throne of power.</note>. For our Emperor, King Christ, won for himself a kingdom upon it, and power in heaven and on earth; he overcame his enemies and reconciled the world to God. This is the banner of the Christian people; this is the sword <note>original: "framea"</note> with which we are strengthened for war against the enemy; this is the insignia of our victory. With this, we trample our enemies.

<header>BOOK TWO</header>

With these weapons of iniquity we break, and through this [the Cross] we are raised to the crown and receive the rewards of virtue. Therefore, O fire of desire <note>In this context, 'cupiditas' refers to worldly lusts or greed that consume the soul.</note>, ever an exile and stranger to what is good, know what destruction is prepared for you in the death of Christ. Thus, those Cherubim, which stood in the construction of the tabernacle and the temple next to the altar behind the altar of Incense <note>original: "altare Thymiamatis"; the altar where fragrant offerings were burnt in the Jewish Temple.</note>, demonstrated this banner of the Cross by the extension of their wings, as well as by the entire position of their placement. These, anointed with mystical oil, prefigured the triumph of Christ and the palm of His struggle. Therefore, these living beings—that is, the Cherubim—rendered joyful, bring forth the deeds of Christ; and they reveal by manifest signs that those deeds are nourishing and sublime. The Seraphim also open their mouths for this purpose: so that when they proclaim that the heavens and the earth are full of the glory of God, the time is now near for carnal luxury to depart from here and for vices to recede. Finally, let all these living beings say together, through the office of their wings, they especially signal that the Savior's arms are stretched out on the Cross. By these arms, all those whom He will later place in the blessed seat at the universal judgment—repaying them according to their merits—are now drawn and lifted up by mercy. Then He will openly prove them through examination, whom He already approved before as known to Him and enriched by good works through His love. Therefore, the prophecies of the righteous seers concerning the passion of the Lord do not disagree in any way, nor do the significations of these living beings deceive.

### On the form of the fifth figure, where four squares stand around the Cross.

<margin>V.</margin>
I now beseech you, O holy Cross of God, that by your power you may bless my weak heart, so that I may be able to sing the trophy of the eternal King upon you with worthy praises: how you join together celestial and earthly things in one treaty, confirm the covenant, and dissolve the bonds of death. O you sacred assembly of Apostles, and laureated order of martyrs: by right you have laid the foundations of the house of Christ, you whom He Himself carries in His most beautiful citadel. Indeed, by your voice and examples, you have acquired a holy people for God, and you have rightly placed the holy and saving Cross of Christ at the very first foundation of your preaching. For the power of the Lord crucified upon it rightly strengthened that entire structure of the Lord’s Church for the bearing of its weight. Truly, it also dedicated the human race to life, and stands as a firm column; desiring to show that through it, the eternal house to be placed in the heavenly kingdom arises—namely, the hall of the just King and the Bridegroom of the Church. By this Cross, O Lord Christ, you have swiftly erected a new trophy in the world by the right of lordship, the blood of redemption, and the path of direction: so that the race of Christ-worshippers may keep the covenant of justice, spurn the rightly damned devil, and overcome the human enemy through piety. For you are for them the favor of praise, the fear of preservation for every good work, the palm of victory, and the crown of reward. O glorious Cross of the Lord, precious foundation of the hall of Christ: you are more beautiful than the flowering appearance of all seeds; you are higher than the Cedars of Lebanon; you are more precious than white Parian stone <note>Paros was famous in antiquity for its high-quality white marble, used for the finest sculptures and temples.</note>. You join together squared stones—the living stones in the firm foundation of faith. The assembly of Patriarchs and the most ancient rite also rightly lay the first foundations at the beginning of the whole building; they who first joined the devoted hearts of those obeying them to the house of God, who reigns over all things, through sound doctrine and faith. ...they might construct [it] in the place of a foundation <note>original: "raminis loco"; likely "straminis loco," meaning a layer or bedding used as a base.</note>: because this entire structure of the Church, through the confession of the name of Jesus Christ, raises us to the heavenly kingdom; and once instructed by His voice, the good construction of a life flourishes properly. ## On the appearance of the Sixth Figure, where the four principal virtues are commemorated.

<margin>VI.</margin>
**O**mnipotent power and supreme wisdom of the omnipotent Father, Christ, Son of God: You are the true Lord, who adorns the entire world with the beauty of the holy Cross, and piously distributes the holy gifts of salvation to Your saints. For the chariot <note>original: "quadriga"; a Roman four-horse chariot. Rabanus uses this image to describe the four cardinal virtues pulling the soul toward heaven.</note> of virtues, fittingly adapted to the four corners of the holy Cross, shows the sacred sequence of types proceeding from it, consecrated in the triumph of King Christ's victory. Through His profitable passion, it is beneficial to the whole world for obtaining the fruit of piety and attaining eternal blessedness. Virtue is a habit of the mind, the glory of nature, the reason of life, the nobility of character, and the moderation of the tongue. Indeed, O holy Cross, you hand down all these things to be approved with just praise by religious men, bringing forth everything pleasing to God and revealing each thing to be wholesome. 

Your holy Prudence taught the tender world from the beginning: when through the martyrdom of the just Abel, it demonstrated that the soul must be laid down for the sake of innocence; from you, Justice, burning with righteous zeal, persuaded us that the devil’s pomp must be spurned and the grace of Christ must be obeyed. Through you, chaste love <note>original: "castus amor"; here representing the spiritual drive of the soul toward God.</note> in the saints of God raises itself to follow useful counsels—that is, the doctrine of God’s commandments—so that it may remove the fraud of the wicked one from the inner chambers of the human heart, and teach the faithful of God, who look toward heavenly rewards, to overcome the desires of the flesh. 

This same love leads holy preachers through the entire breadth of the world, rebuking vices and commending virtues. They teach that thanks must be given through the Gospel to the Redeemer, who, according to the prophecy of the ancients, was incarnate in the final times; by delivering the commands of the Gospel through signs and miracles, He became known as the true God. He granted to all who are faithful to Him that they might seek eternal light through full faith and baptism. To those who received the heavenly doctrine with attentive ears, He gave the power to bring forth an abundant fruit of virtues from the seed of the Word, in the manner of good soil. If any impulses of [fallen] nature should arise in them, once cut away by the knife of the Gospel <note>original: "Euangelij cultro"</note>, the flame of the Holy Spirit would burn them away, so that without any impediment they might present the divine sprout and spiritual delights to King Christ. 

First, faith and the Christian religion planted these fruits through the preachers of the Gospel; then the grace of virtues showed them to be pure and free from all filth; thereafter, the patience of the saints proved them in tribulations. The covenant and society of true concord established them by demonstrating they were joined and inseparable. From there, they are strongly fortified by the virtue of constancy, and through true humility they are kept unharmed, so that through discernment <note>original: "discretionem"; the ability to distinguish between good and evil impulses.</note> they may be able to grow, and through long-suffering perseverance come to a fitting maturity.

### ->On the formation of the seventh figure, where the four elements are discussed.<-

<margin>VII</margin>
Therefore, all things that are in the heavens and on the earth now shine, illuminated by the light of Christ’s glory; they serve His majesty as subjects and celebrate the achievement of the holy Cross by blessing it, so that they may pay their due vows to the heavenly victor. They truly profess that all kingdoms maintain their proper order under the governance of the divinity of Jesus <note>original: "Hieſu"; a medieval spelling of Jesus.</note>. Not only those things that move within the world, but indeed all things that exist, live, feel, and discern, and know how to keep laws, have stood under this command from the beginning. Rain also and hail from the clouds, snow, frost and ice, dew and clear weather, together with the springs and streams flowing on the earth, praise the Creator by bearing witness to Him. The Cretan Bear <note>original: "Arctos Creticus"; a poetic name for the constellation Ursa Major, the Great Bear. Let the just man say in praise that Christ, exalted on the Cross, draws all things to Himself and invites His chosen soldiers to the crown. For it is not right that His handiwork should disagree in praising the Creator, but rather, rejoicing, it should sing the praises due to Him in harmony. All things swimming in the waters and creeping on the earth, mountains and hills, the sand of the sea, groves and all the trees of the forests, wild beasts, cattle, and fierce animals, dusty worms, and tiny flying things, tame birds and those that tear with their talons. O Christian race, by whom the heavens and earth are adorned, from you the light of faith and the power of preaching comes forth, acting as an embassy to the nations, stirring up prayers, and inviting people to baptism; but especially the speech of teachers, by its noble exhortation, strips bare the devil’s deceit and explains Christ’s victory to the elect acquired through God’s grace. To all the faithful, this is preached daily, and it is also made known with the utmost modesty and patience to pagans, false Christians, and heretics. He who believes the word of God shall be saved; but he who does not believe or destroys faith by wicked works shall be condemned forever. Therefore, because the grace of Christ overflows in the heavens and on the earth, it is very fitting that celestial and earthly beings alike should sing praises to God with one voice and give thanks. People of the Lord and sheep of His pasture, you who partly reign now with the Lord in the heavens and partly still wander as pilgrims on the earth: one purpose incites you to praise God, for one joy awaits you in the heavens. For what has been given you already hold, and what has been promised you shall truly receive; for He who promised will undoubtedly fulfill His promises in you, namely your own King and Priest, Creator and Savior, Jesus Christ our Lord.

O Christ, Son of God, Almighty Power and the supreme wisdom of the almighty Father: You are the true Lord, who adorns the whole world with the beauty of the holy Cross, and piously dispenses the holy gifts of salvation to Your saints. Therefore, because the grace of Christ overflows in the heavens and on the earth, it is well-fitting that heavenly and earthly beings alike, with a harmonious voice, should sing praises to God and give thanks. O people of the Lord and sheep of his pasture—you who in part already reign with the Lord in the heavens, and you who in part still wander as pilgrims on the earth—one single reason stirs you to praise God, for one single joy awaits you in the heavens. For what has been given, you already hold; and what has been promised, you shall truly receive; because he who promised will without doubt fulfill his promises in you: he who is your own King and Priest, Creator and Savior, Jesus Christ our Lord.

<margin>VI.</margin>
O Christ, Son of God, Almighty power and supreme wisdom of the almighty Father: you are the true Lord who adorns the whole world with the beauty of the Holy Cross, and you piously dispense the holy gifts of salvation to your saints. For the chariot <note>original: "quadriga"; referring to the four-horse chariot used in Roman triumphs, here a metaphor for the four cardinal virtues.</note> of virtues, fittingly adapted to the four corners of the Holy Cross, shows the sacred sequence of forms proceeding from it, consecrated in the triumph of the victory of Christ the King: and through his passion, it is profitable to the whole world for obtaining the fruit of piety and attaining eternal blessedness. Virtue is a habit of the mind, the beauty of nature, the reason of life, the nobility of character, and the moderation of the tongue. All these things, O Holy Cross, you hand down to be approved with just praise by religious men: bringing forth all things together that are pleasing to God, and showing each one to be soul-healing. Your holy prudence taught the tender world from the beginning: when, through the martyrdom of the just Abel, it demonstrated that the soul must be laid down for the sake of innocence; from you, justice, burning well with zeal, persuaded us that the devil’s display must be scorned and the grace of Christ must be obeyed. Through you, chaste love in the saints of God raises itself to pursue useful counsels—that is, the doctrine of the commandments of God—so that it may remove the fraud of the wicked one from the inner chambers of the human heart, and teach the faithful of God, who are looking toward heavenly rewards, to overcome the lusts of the flesh. That same love leads holy preachers through the entire breadth of the world, rebuking vices and commending virtues: teaching through the Gospel that thanks must be given to the Redeemer, who according to the prophecy of the ancients was incarnated in the last times, and handing down the evangelical commandments, became known as the true God through signs and miracles. He granted to all who are faithful to him that they might seek eternal light through full faith and baptism; and to those who received the heavenly doctrine with attentive ears, he gave them the power to bring forth an abundant fruit of virtues from the seed of the Word, in the manner of good soil. And if any incentives of [fallen] nature should arise in them, being pruned away by the knife of the Gospel, the flame of the Holy Spirit would burn them up: so that without any impediment they might offer the divine offspring and spiritual delights to Christ the King. Therefore, faith and the Christian religion first planted these fruits through the preachers of the Gospel; then the grace of virtues showed them to be pure and foreign to all filth; then the patience of the saints proved them in tribulations; the covenant also and the fellowship of true concord established them by showing them united and inseparable; thereafter they are strongly fortified by the virtue of constancy, and are kept unharmed through true humility, so that through discernment they may be able to advance toward increase, and through long-suffering perseverance reach a fitting maturity. After these things...

...Indeed, the sickle of the final judgment must now be sent out: so that the whitening harvest, which the grain of wheat <note>A reference to John 12:24; Christ is the "grain of wheat" who died to produce a great harvest.</note>—buried in the earth through the plow of the Cross—has produced in a glorious and multiplied form, may be gathered by the ministry of Angels when the Judge of the living and the dead appears; and through the sentence of that same just Judge, may be happily gathered into the heavenly granaries.

### *On the formation of the seventh figure, where the four elements are discussed.*

<margin>VII.</margin>
**T**herefore, all things in heaven and on earth, illuminated by the light of Christ’s glory, now shine forth. They serve his majesty in subjection and celebrate the achievement of the Holy Cross with blessings, so that they may pay their due vows to the heavenly victor. They truly profess that all kingdoms maintain their proper order under the governance of the divinity of Jesus <note>original: "Hiesu"; a common medieval spelling variant of Jesus.</note>; not only those things which move within the world, but even all things that exist, live, feel, and discern, and know how to keep laws, have stood under this command from the beginning. The rain also and the hail from the clouds, the snow, frost and ice, the dew and the clear sky, together with the springs and streams flowing upon the earth, praise the Creator as his witnesses. The Cretan Bear <note>original: "Arctos Creticus"; a classical poetic name for the constellations Ursa Major and Ursa Minor, which revolve around the celestial pole and were used by sailors for navigation.</note> and every arrangement of the stars, along with the turning of the pole, proclaim their author. Let no one be displeased by what I say, for I am writing the praises of the Almighty, and I do not intend to cause mockery or grief to anyone. Bless the Lord, all you works of the Lord: sing and play psalms to him. Let the righteous person say in praise that Christ, exalted on the Cross, draws all things to himself, and invites his chosen soldiers to the crown. For it is not right that the thing created should disagree in praising its maker, but rather it should harmoniously sing the praises due to him with joy. All things swimming in the waters and the creeping things of the earth, mountains and hills, the sand of the sea, groves and all the trees of the forests, wild animals, livestock, and fierce beasts, dust-crawling worms, and tiny flying things, tame birds and those that tear with their claws. O Christian race, by whom the heavens and earth are adorned, from you the light of faith and the power of preaching go forth, performing a mission to the nations, stirring up prayers, and inviting people to baptism. But most of all, the speech of the teachers, with noble exhortation, strips bare the deceit of the devil and explains the victory of Christ to the elect gathered through the grace of God. This is preached daily to all the faithful, and it is also made known with the greatest modesty and patience to the pagans, false Christians, and heretics. He, therefore, who believes in the word of God shall be saved; but he who does not believe, or who destroys his faith with wicked works, shall be damned for eternity. Therefore, because the grace of Christ overflows in heaven and on earth, he will surely grant that the heavenly and earthly things together, with a harmonious voice, may sing praises to God and give thanks. People of the Lord and sheep of his pasture, you who partly reign already with the Lord in heaven, and partly still travel as pilgrims on earth: one single purpose incites you to praise God, for whom one single joy waits in the heavens. For what has been given, you already hold; and what has been promised, you shall truly receive, because he who promised will without doubt fulfill his promises in you—namely, your own King and Priest, Creator and Savior, Jesus Christ our Lord.

# BOOK TWO.
<i>[Signature mark i]</i>

<margin>VIII.</margin> And so Christ our Savior, Christ the mildest king, reigns in the heavens, the best counsel: the highest power of God the Father, and true blessing, light from light, and divine offspring begotten from God the parent. From here, evidently, is the origin of all law: to this master-craftsman the entire fabric of heaven and earth looks; to him belongs all the beauty of virtues. From his goodness and truth every good and true thing exists, and he himself, alone wonderful, performs wonders. By his justice, whatever is justly decreed, approved, and brought forth in heaven or on earth is ordered: whatever honor the good Angels possess, and whatever punishment the evil Angels suffer. Furthermore, it was Christ who drove idolatry from the world and renewed divine worship. The Lord Christ is therefore the author of all these good things, who demonstrates the judgments of his own honor and power in the banner of his Cross. Wherefore it is fitting that we, the earth-born and exiles of paradise, should mark these rays which this form of the Holy Cross diffuses; through which Christ saves us and restores the splendor of light, which the first-formed man <note>original: "protoplastus"; a Greek-derived term for Adam, the first-created human.</note>, sinning once, had long ago lost. Therefore, as many as from the beginning have worshiped while rightly acknowledging these rays, they enjoy the gift of perpetual light. Frequently the weapons of the Prophets vibrated with this radiance, and perhaps the Apostolic preaching flashed nobly with this light; by this sun, the faith of Christ shines back throughout the whole world, and the good hearts of men and the pious vows of the saints lie open. The just also, prevailing by divine gift through mystical signs once delivered to the fathers, perceive a good and salvific ray; and thereafter they persuade the peoples to obey the commands of God, since they ascribe to Christ alone the power to reveal the depth of mysteries to the worthy and to deliver the gifts of eternal life to the faithful. Christ, therefore, the highest king and Lord bestowing celestial things by divine gift, climbing the high timbers of the Cross, thundered forth manifest truths by forming this shape; through it, he opens the heavens to the world, and he desires that we, following the footsteps of his life, may find the entrance through it. Finally, the twelve winds <note>original: "quater ternos ventos" - literally "four times three winds." Classical tradition often divided the winds into twelve directions.</note> from the four quarters of the world and the circuit of the ocean, joined and united in the form of the holy Cross, the Savior has made healthy. The Ruler himself, sustaining the twelve signs of the zodiac with their twelve months, rules and governs them; he disposes the twelve spaces of the hours, as the sun rises, to be drawn and led in an orderly way to the setting. To demonstrate all these things, the distribution of the number twelve <term>duodenarius</term> <note>The number twelve was considered a "perfect" number representing the intersection of the spiritual (3) and the material (4), used here to link the Cross to the structure of time and space.</note> completes the quadrangular form of the holy Cross. For all the chains of our sins, by which we were held bound, are loosed by the cross of Christ—our glory—and the upright Cross itself proposes and marks the sacred joys of heaven and the laws of the earth; it praises and approves them, and truly confers them upon the faithful.

### *On the ninth figure, which contains the number of the days of the year in the form of the Cross.*

<margin>IX.</margin> Sun and Moon, behold, now in fitting order bless the Lord Jesus <note>original: "Hiesum"; a common medieval spelling variant.</note> Christ: because the holy Cross is your honor, your stable light, your arranged order, sequence, praise, and integrity, illuminating you through all times with spiritual light. You also, by this boundary—which the Cross portends in four hexagons and a single unit <note>original: "monade"; the number one or a single point in the center of a geometric arrangement.</note> placed between them—count out the days and nights of the whole solar year; and it balances your course to the perfection of that number. The aforementioned figure of it, therefore, contains within itself thirty times ten [300] and ten times six [60], and furthermore five times unity [5] <note>This describes the mathematical composition of the grid for Figure IX, totaling 365, the number of days in a solar year.</note>. ### BOOK TWO.

...the wheel of the Sun and Moon is known to instill its course through numbers; the four changes of the seasons are included in these: all of which one year equally embraces in fifty-two weeks and a single day <note>original: "monade"; referring to the single day left over in a solar year after 52 weeks.</note>. This order holds the return of the two-faced month <note>original: "bifrontis"; a reference to Janus, the two-faced god of January, marking the new year.</note> to this day; to this day passes the series of hours, the change of seasons, the yearly circuit, and the course of the stars. And the extra quarter of hours beyond the fixed number of days—which the holy Cross denotes in the arrangement of the six angles and four hexagons—quickly reaches that boundary, which can be rightly discerned in the equinoxes. 

O sacred shoot, you who illuminate with the clear light of faith and wisdom the hearts of men set in the darkness of infidelity: you are clearly the holy Cross, flashing with miracles. For from here, Christ demonstrates the breadth of his kingdom everywhere through your horns <note>original: "cornua"; the projecting arms or points of the Cross, signifying power and reach.</note>. You are the scepter of the strongest king and the altar of God most high, spread through the world by a powerful order: you descended to the depths; you reach toward the heavens. This is the glory and honor of the whole world. 

Our same true Shem <note>original: "Sem"; the name of Noah's son, used here as a symbolic title for Christ, likely meaning "The Name."</note> likewise named, through whose name alone the whole creation is saved, tempers the course of the stars to the form of this Cross, and gives the kingdom of heaven itself; since, placed on this seat, he opens the gates of heaven to us. Indeed, the human race, praising this in song, explains: when it faithfully proclaims that for Christ, who was crucified by the Jews, the light of the stars was darkened at midday. For though Judea seethed, gnashing with envy, yet by a better use it brought forth this fruit on the tree of the Cross: so that from the four regions of the world and from the fourfold border of the Ocean, nations and peoples flowing together from every side might seek the spiritual delights which are shown in the holy Cross. Thus, filled with sacred and mystic feasts, they might through the gifts of the highest Father reach the hundredfold fruit of good works; and, joined with the splendid nine orders of Angels, they might themselves shine with perpetual clarity in celestial bliss. 

Therefore I advise: that whatever we sing and whatever we write, we turn it all to the praise of the Redeemer. Thus, by this one hope which we have through him and in him, we may repel the end of greedy and raging death and eternal damnation with the shield of faith, and escape. And so, shining with heavenly light, may we joyfully deserve to possess the kingdom of God, and resound with worthy praises of our author and redeemer, the Lord Jesus Christ—the son of the almighty Father, true, holy, and the highest Lord. May this always be our reasoning, our everlasting praise, and the perpetual fire of love.

->*On the reasoning of the tenth figure, where the ratio of seventy is described.*<-

<margin>X.</margin>
Now therefore it is fitting that a pious melody, gladdening us with the hope of eternal things, should express in this blessed work what confers eternal life upon us, and what takes away corruption; what grants forgiveness of sins, and what breaks the chains of our transgressions: that is, let it preach the acts of the holy Cross. Rightly, therefore, does the human voice resound this in the throat; this is brought forth by the skill of the speaking mouth, the writing fingers, the plectrum of the tongue, and the vows of a pious heart: that the twisted and harmful dragon fell in war. That savage one, who with malignant art deceived our First-formed <note>original: "Protoplastum"; referring to Adam, the first-created human.</note> in paradise, when earlier Lucifer himself, falling from the citadel of heaven, dragged a third part of the stars with him to the sulfurous pools of hell; because, proud and deceitful, he attempted to make himself equal to the Most High, placing his throne in the cold part of the North <note>original: "Aquilonis"; in medieval theology, the North was associated with the seat of Satan’s rebellion (based on Isaiah 14).</note>.

...tribunal. Truly, the most mild lamb <note>original: "agnus mitissimus"; a reference to Christ</note> laid low this most fierce wolf <note>original: "ferocissimum lupum"; a reference to the Devil</note>, by right snatched the prey from the powerful one, and shattered his monstrous efforts. But the Gentiles, through the holy preaching of the Gospel, He converted from deep and carnal desires to better things, and inflamed them toward heavenly gifts: so that neither the fabulous superstition of the Jews, nor the perverse seduction of the heretics, might corrupt the chaste hearts of Christians with a fair-seeming veil. These Christians, recognizing the truth of the divine law, now stand firm in the strength of faith. And lest the mouth of the nations—emptied of the cult of demons and the adoration of idols—become parched, Christ the Lord, the author of all good and the giver of virtues, makes it fruitful in divine praise. For the powerful virtue of the holy Cross accuses and condemns all the treachery of the enemy; and by releasing the world from its debts, it excels all the wealth of the rich by its own gift. Finally, the Prophet Daniel demonstrates that manifest redemption for the whole world would occur in the number seventy <note>original: "septuagenario numero"</note>, in his seventy weeks which reached all the way to Christ: when transgression is finished, sin takes its end, iniquity is blotted out, and everlasting justice is brought in. Jeremiah likewise predicts that the release from captivity would come after seventy years. Furthermore, Moses, through the seventy elders whom he placed over the people of Israel by the Lord’s command, signified that the perfection of all mastery and the revelation of mysteries is made for us through the sacrament of the Cross. O blessed Cross of God: in this, you embrace the number seventy divided into five parts in your middle, and likewise through your four horns by the numbers four and ten <note>original: "quaternario, et denario numero"; likely referring to the four arms of the cross multiplied by the ten of the Decalogue</note>, signifying that you recall the whole world to the harmony and unity of faith through the ten commandments of the law <note>original: "decalogum legis"</note> and through the four books of the holy Gospel. Nor do you pass over the number five <note>original: "quinarium"</note> without a mystery: but you venerably hint that the human race is most truly devoted to you, not only through the internal affection of the mind, but also through the external senses of the body.

## On the eleventh figure, where the Pentateuch of Moses is arranged.

<margin>XI.</margin>
I invoke You, holy Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that You may be my teacher and guide in this poem; and to this work now begun, grant sense to the maker in Your piety and mercy, providing sober words so that I may faithfully unfold—to the eternal praise of the holy Cross and to the glory of the New Testament—what the ancient law signified through figures that are now, in this time of grace, to be observed spiritually in the things themselves. For when first this great machine of the universe was made visible from the invisible and impenetrable depth, and Paradise appeared flourishing and pleasant with its budding growth, immediately in the Tree of Life, which is in the midst of Paradise, the life-giving wood of the holy Cross was prefigured. Positioned in the midst of the nations, it vivifies and sanctifies the generations that go before and follow it; by its benefit, all good and holy men are restored, bringing forth the spiritual and vital fruits of virtues. Isaac the Patriarch also prefigured this wood of Christ’s passion when, with his father placing it upon him, he carried the wood on his own shoulders to the place of his sacrifice, as the book of Genesis testifies. So too Exodus and the other books of the Law explain that the holy Cross, with its strong framework of arms, has carried away our price: so that by the dowry of His own blood, the heavenly Bridegroom might present to Himself a bride, the Church, having neither spot nor wrinkle. From here, the people of the Israelites, joined to God in Egypt and led across the Red Sea, sang victorious praises to their Redeemer; and walking a journey of three days, to the Lord merci-

### On the reasoning of the twelfth figure, where the name of the First-Formed is located.
<note>original: "Proto-plasti"; a Greek-derived term for Adam, the "first-formed" human.</note>

<margin>XII.</margin>
Come now, sweet-sounding pipe of the metric art, go to sing the health-bringing praise of the Lord's cross in sweet verses: and celebrate with devoted praises the wonderful work of our redemption, as well as the consolation of the future life: because on the holy cross most cruel death was conquered, and the chains of sins were loosened. The ancient light has returned to us through Christ: and pardon for the first transgression was granted. For the first Adam took the beauty of immortality away from us when he tasted the apple of the forbidden tree against the command: and the second Adam, namely our Savior, coming to us, brought with him all the beauty, and all the glory and honor of heavenly brightness. Because of the fault of one, we suffered many and innumerable evils, and fell into the dangers of temporal death: so by the grace of one, the faithful ranks are saved, and possess eternal light. Finally, just as through the wood of transgression death entered into the whole world, and all descended into hell, even the chosen themselves: so also through the wood of the Lord's passion death was taken captive, and many escaped from it, even those liable for sins. Through this, he revealed to us the secret of his sacrament: and had established a pact with us to keep the law of his will. The first man, earthly from the earth, generated earthly offspring, for whom he also inherited death: also the second, heavenly from heaven, brought a heavenly generation to the world: and promised eternal blessedness to his followers. ### *On the reasoning of the Thirteenth Figure, where that number of days is included which Christ spent in the womb of the Virgin.*

<margin>XIII</margin>
O Tree of sweetest scent and widest expansion of beautiful branches, an incomparable and flowing garden of delights! Most pleasant in your vast abundance, with the flowers of virtues and the leaves of words, you bring forth fruit through the preachers of the Holy Gospel and store up heavenly riches. Indeed, you exist as an honorable and decorous thing, exalted in majesty above all the trees of the forest; for the brightness of Christ crucified upon you has displayed you as glorious, beautiful, and venerable to all. Whoever stands firm in the strength of faith professes this with full devotion, even though the horrific power of the demon—envying this salvation—has hitherto resisted the nations' efforts to believe and know it. Indeed, you demonstrate various types of virtues in your form, and you signify that you possess an abundance of spiritual riches; you shine with the purple glow of Christ's blood, and you strongly persuade us to lay down our souls for Christ. In you consists the high dignity of the Savior’s Churches, and the unity of the faithful shall remain in faith and peace. This was even prefigured by the erection of the Mosaic Tabernacle or the building of the Solomonic Temple; this was signified by the altar of burnt offerings and the altar of incense <note>original: "thymiamatis"</note>, and the fire always burning upon them. This too was indicated by the lampstand with four lamps and the rest of the Sabbath; for in Christ—namely the unspotted Lamb of God, sacrificed for our salvation on the altar of the Cross—there is the illumination and the perpetual rest of the saints. He himself is our guide to life through the passion of the Cross; he is eternal salvation, he is the true light, he is the most pious goodness, he is our redemption, he is also everlasting life. He is the prince, like a son in his own house—namely the Holy Church. He is our peace, who has made both one; he has destroyed the principality of the devil and slowed his harmful efforts. The devil strives to extinguish the fervor of charity through the cold of infidelity, and by the allurements of pleasures, he deceitfully promises true happiness, mocking those already captured through this madness, binding them with the manifest bonds of vices and the chains of sins. O holy Cross, O beautiful tree, you who surpass all the groves of cedars in incomparable height and beauty: behold, with a fitting number radiating in your points <note>original: "cornibus," literally 'horns,' referring to the ends of the cross-bar</note>, you portend most serene and blessed gifts through the Lord's coming. For you show the sequence of days in which the Savior was incarnate in the womb of the Virgin; and through this delay, you offer us documents of his patience and humility. Because he came to us with gentleness and tranquility through birth, you designate his mildness and obedience, which he preserved even unto the death carried out upon you. ### *On the Fourteenth Figure, in which the number of years from the beginning of the world until the year of the Passion of Christ is noted.*

<margin>14</margin>
Truly it is a worthy and most distinguished work to sing the trophy of the heavenly King with sweet-sounding melody: to fittingly proclaim the triumph of the eternal Ruler, by which He snatched the world from the power of the Tyrant <note>The "Tyrant" refers to the Devil.</note>, and, having destroyed and rejected his kingdom, condemned him to eternal prison. In this triumph, He also supports and sustains the things of heaven, earth, and sea through the kingdom He has acquired for Himself. For when His exaltation occurred, starting from the origin of the nascent world, the running count of the years expresses this through the Greek numerals <note>original: "notas Græcorum"</note> arranged in the figure itself. Because of this, the devotion of believers increases when they perceive how the Creator of all things fits the sequence of time so harmoniously and appropriately to the events themselves: namely, that the figure of the Cross and the redemption performed upon it, as well as the salvation bestowed upon the faithful through the gifts of the virtues, rightly agree in all things with a number full of sacred mysteries.

Furthermore, the beginning of the book of Genesis most clearly proves and confirms that the Lord renewed the ancient ages and His creation—which He had established in the beginning—through the Holy Cross near the end of time. For while God is said to have rested after the six days of work and the creation of man, the Redeemer is shown to have rested in the tomb on the Sabbath <note>The seventh day of the week, Saturday.</note> after man was restored through the Cross in the sixth age of the world <note>In medieval historiography, the "Sixth Age" began with the birth of Christ and continues to the present.</note> and on the sixth day of the week <note>Friday, the day of the Crucifixion.</note>. Therefore, by divine will, it was arranged that the number 5,231 <note>original: "V.CC.XXX.I."</note> would aptly suit the figure of the Holy Cross. Through this, it demonstrates that the sacrament of Christ’s passion resists all the wickedness of demons and the falsehood of depraved men; it overwhelms them with power and overcomes with justice anyone who, by fraud or deceit, would detract from the plan of the Lord’s incarnation. Let all the cleverness of philosophers and heretics be utterly silenced by the conviction of this truth! No longer should the deceitful faction of the Jews oppose their dire and cruel disposition to the Gospel of Christ: for He is the power of God for the salvation of everyone who believes. Through this, the will of the Creator is made clear, and it is demonstrated that the Holy Cross sanctifies all the times of the world for God’s elect who have existed from the beginning. It promises the heavenly kingdom, which will be granted by our Redeemer to all the faithful who, obedient to His word with a believing heart and pure works, have strived to please God. Indeed, the sight of the Holy Cross is a great consolation to the faithful and provides material for praise, because it makes us know the goodness of the Creator. He had first formed man upright in Paradise, and now, unwilling for him to perish by the fraud of the ancient enemy <note>The Serpent/Satan.</note>, He recovers him through the Cross and leads him back to Paradise. The Cross is indeed the citadel of virtues <note>original: "arx virtutum"</note> and the remission of sins; it raises all people from these low and fleeting things to heavenly and sublime heights—those whom Christ’s election has proven worthy of the eternal vision of God through Faith, Hope, and Charity.

### *On the logic of the Thirteenth Figure, in which the number of days is included, during which Christ remained in the womb of the Virgin.*

<margin>13</margin>
O Tree of sweetest fragrance and widest reach of beautiful branches, an incomparable garden of overflowing delights, most pleasant in the abundant richness of the flowers of virtue and the leaves of words, bearing fruit through the preachers of the holy Gospel, you store up heavenly riches. Indeed, exalted in majesty above all the trees of the forests, you exist as honorable and beautiful: because the brightness of Christ crucified upon you has displayed you as glorious, lovely, and venerable to all. Whoever stands firm in the strength of faith professes this with full devotion, even though the horrid force of the demon—envying that the nations should believe and know this salvation—has resisted until now. You demonstrate various kinds of virtues in your form, and you signify that you possess an abundance of spiritual riches; you shine with a purple gleam from the blood of Christ, and you strongly persuade us to lay down our lives for Christ’s sake. In you, the high dignity of the Savior’s Churches consists, and the unity of the faithful will remain in faith and peace—which was even prefigured by the raising of the Mosaic tabernacle or the building of Solomon’s temple. He Himself is our forerunner to life through the passion of the Cross; He is eternal salvation, He is the true light, He is the most pious goodness, He is our redemption, and He is everlasting life. He is the prince, like a son in his own house—that is, the holy Church. He is our peace, who has made both one; He destroyed the princedom of the devil and hindered his harmful attempts. The devil strives to extinguish the heat of charity through the cold of infidelity, and by promising true happiness through the allurements of pleasures, he deceives as a liar; and mocking man as if already captured through this madness, he binds him with the manifest bonds of vices and the chains of sins. O holy Cross, O beautiful tree, you who surpass all the groves of cedars in incomparable height and beauty: behold, in the appropriate number radiating in your corners, you portend the most serene and blessed gifts through the Lord’s coming. For you show the sequence of days in which the Savior was incarnated in the womb of the Virgin; and through this delay, you provide us with documents of His patience and humility. And because He came to us through birth with gentleness and tranquility, you designate His mildness and obedience, which He preserved even unto the death carried out upon you. Therefore, all power in heaven and on earth has been given to Him according to His humanity—He who, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, created heaven and earth and all things that are in them according to His divinity. Just as the holy Prophets sang long ago: that the Maker of heaven and earth would be born as a small son, whose government should be upon his shoulder <note>A reference to Isaiah 9:6, interpreted here as Christ carrying the Cross on His shoulder.</note>.

<margin>XVII.</margin>
O holy and blessed, powerful and venerable Cross of Christ, praise of the future life and glory of the Redeemer, you are indeed a prosperous work and vital to all ages from the beginning, kind and honorable. For when you fatigued the limbs of Christ suspended in his passion <note>original: "passione"; the physical suffering of the crucifixion</note> upon you, you rescued innumerable peoples from the darkness of their sins, and mercifully returned through grace the kingdom of heaven which had been taken away through transgression. For the goodness of the Creator did not allow those who had long held hope in him to perish, but through you he rewarded their good merits, namely by granting them an eternal crown. For the seed of Gospel teaching, which the Savior sowed in the hearts of his disciples, he multiplied in their work according to his pleasure when, sitting on the mountain, he taught them. Beginning from the eight beatitudes <note>The blessings listed by Jesus at the start of the Sermon on the Mount</note>, he brought forth the most generous teachings, certainly hinting at them through the most fitting number of the figure of the Holy Cross <note>Likely referring to a numerical or geometric correlation between the eight beatitudes and the structure of the cross in this specific manuscript's diagrams</note>, because the Holy Cross is the bringer of virtues, and the beginning and perfection of our salvation, and through it our salvation and resurrection are achieved. 

So therefore it is fitting, and thus, O whoever you are among the number of the righteous, as long as you are here, bring forth divine praise with fear and love, do works of justice, forgive your enemy who persecutes you, and provide him relief. Kindly receive Christ’s poor, who now mourn in the present age, and those hungering and thirsting for justice <note>original: "iustitiam"; often translated as righteousness in this context</note>, who pant with all desire for the future life, because they are pricked by divine inspiration and, having their hearts set on things above, they contemplate who rules all things by eternal counsel and who forgives sins by immense mercy. I, a wretched man, describe this in the Latin language, and I desire this: that he himself may be the refreshment of my mind in the present, and eternal satiety <note>fullness/satisfaction</note> in the future. For no proud person will be justified from here by showing humility only in mouth and habit <note>original: "habit"; referring to outward appearance or monastic clothing</note>, and the heavenly ruler...

# BOOK TWO

A person may prostrate themselves on the ground in worship, yet if their heart remains proud, or if they possess riches but do not give alms, or if they have bodily health (being a man of full strength) yet do not perform works of justice, they do nothing. For it is certain and clear that the all-holding Creator seeks not only words, but also good deeds and an honest life at all times. Therefore, whoever truly seeks the eternal light and wishes to arrive at eternal blessedness must tend toward the heavenly kingdom through the eight Evangelical titles <note>original: "octo titulos Euangelicos"; these are the eight Beatitudes from the Sermon on the Mount</note> in which the forms of true blessedness are expressed. Indeed, in that very number <note>The number eight often symbolized the Resurrection and the "eighth day" of eternity</note>, once the general resurrection is accomplished and the judgment finished, the saints of God will enter the eternal kingdom together with Christ. The Cross of Christ is also the way of the righteous, an ascent to heaven, a wheel pulling us from the depths to the heights, the leader and the gate of the kingdom, and our victory. Through it, we shall possess true life and receive an eternal reward. The Cross also contains the number eight within itself (formed by four multiplied by two), signifying that through the two precepts of charity <note>Love of God and love of neighbor</note> which the four holy books of the Gospels commend to us, we can earn everlasting joys. This also the almighty Spirit of the almighty God—who invites us through peace and true charity to the future kingdom—placed as steps of ascent in our hearts through the seven gifts of his grace. He did this to demonstrate that the faithful can rightly ascend to heaven in this manner, provided they do not neglect to become participants in his grace; and that glory and a bright crown upon a heavenly throne await them above, whom true charity has illuminated here with virtue.

->*Concerning the eighteenth figure, where the number forty is placed.*<-

<margin>XVIII.</margin>
Set forth now, O man, and proclaim with praise—with the full affection of your soul and all the senses of your body—the noble triumph of the eternal Victor. The glory of the Lord's Cross displays this triumph everywhere: above the high stars of the heavens and beneath the deepest pits of the abyss, where the brightness of eternal light remains and where the horror of perpetual night endures. It is shown throughout all the reaches of the earth, where night and day alternate in their distinct turns until the end of the world arrives. Let the intellect of the mind meditate on this, let the throat resound with the voice, let the tongue strike against the palate, let the hand write it in letters, let the lips express it in words, and let this very figure, depicted in a metrical work, mark it down. Although it is difficult, this figure brings forth the clear praises of the holy Cross, arranged and modeled through the number forty <note>original: "quadragenarium"; the number 40 traditionally represents the period of trial or the duration of the world</note> divided into four decades. This number, full of venerable mystery and serene with heavenly light, carries among the other sacraments of its meaning the image of the present time. In this time, the holy Church under Christ the Prince fights bravely and insuperably against spiritual wickednesses and against lovers of the world, using the shield of faith, the breastplate of justice, the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit (that is, the word of God). Trusting in the power of her King and conscious of his virtue, she breaks and casts down all the fiery arrows of the ancient enemy. Indeed, with the banner of the Cross—which the victorious Church gloriously carries marked upon her forehead—she confounds the front of the opposing side and suddenly disturbs the savage battle line of her enemies. Therefore, our Savior had conquered the ancient enemy on the holy Cross, and in the number rightly and aptly fitting its figure—namely, forty—he extended his sacred fast in the desert. He did this so that he might first conquer the most fraudulent thief through patience and humility when he first tempted him, and then, as the enemy persisted and endured in his wickedness, Christ might justly damn him to eternal death by his own dying. Just as...

IX.

HEADER: BOOK TWO

...filled <note>original: "impleuit"; this catchword from the previous page completes a thought about Christ fulfilling the law</note>. For just as that slippery and cunning serpent first enticed man to crime through gluttony, greed, and vainglory, and thus rendered him subject to death: so, on the contrary, with fitting medicines, our Savior raised the human race to life through abstinence, kindness, and humility. As victor, he subjected the very author of death <note>Satan</note>, guilty of eternal torments, to the abyss <note>original: "tartaro"</note>. Christ's fight is our victory, and his triumph is our salvation; he who sits in the high citadel of the heavens and looks down upon the lower parts of the earth. His Cross itself is the honor of the whole world; it sustains the entire world, and may it remain forever venerable to me in song and love: praise always in my mouth, and perpetual exultation in my heart.

### Concerning the nineteenth form, where the logic of the number fifty is explained.

<margin>19</margin>
Pay attention with your eyes and see with your mind, hear with your ears and perceive with your heart, O all you faithful, in whom the charity of Christ and the love of wisdom burns: you who care to reach the eternal light and receive incorruption and immortality without end. I bring forth the praise of the Cross of Christ in song. Here the power of the highest Creator <note>original: "summi opificis"</note> is shown, and the beauty of the blessed work is expressed; the nobility of the Artist himself is declared. Your honor is not fleeting, but remains perpetual according to the order of redemption: your palm of victory in heaven is immortal, because Christ himself is your victory, who—truly existing as our salvation—turned back the vengeance upon the ancient enemy, and tasting death upon the Cross, conquered the very author of death.

Come together here, all you who are sick, and let it not shame you to complain of your troubles to him. He is your true physician, whom the holy Cross carried upon the visible wood: he himself invites you to his healing with his hands spread wide, he who swiftly grants you complete health. Open to him the wound of the mind, and do not hide the poison lurking in the ulcer of the body: ask for healing with the devotion of the heart, and knock upon the Physician with the vigor of good works. His health-giving hand does not know how to linger in the delay of time, but is capable, in the speed of a moment, of granting health to all who are healthfully struck with fear and who desire with reverence to be cured by the true Physician himself. He possesses the highest power to perfect a cure and wise counsel to provide salvation; he who descended from the heavenly and eternal to the lowly and temporal, so that he might restore the nature of things (which had been corrupted) by divine dispensation, so that the fear of death might depart, and the signs of blessedness might be demonstrated again in man through divine gifts <note>original: "charismata"</note>.

Therefore, the form of the holy Cross notes in its "horns" <note>The ends or points of the cross</note>—venerably inscribed—that the number fifty is health-giving for us, and rightly designates that it is full of heavenly mysteries <note>original: "sacramentis"</note>. For in that number, knowledge of the true Jubilee <note>A year of total release or remission occurring every 50 years in the Old Testament</note>—that is, of full remission—is given: in it, the Sabbath rest is rightly celebrated. That number is distinguished by the giving of the Old Law; and even more distinguished by the arrival of the Spirit, the Comforter <note>original: "Spiritus paracliti"; referring to the Holy Spirit's descent at Pentecost, fifty days after the Resurrection</note> upon the Apostles. It reveals that the Author of Peace has come, and shows the seal of peace through the perfect reconciliation between God and men by the grace of the Holy Spirit. It is venerable in appearance, healthful in shape, and perfect in the beauty of its mysteries. For the letter X is most fitting for the figure of the holy Cross, and designating the number ten <note>In Roman numerals, X stands for ten</note>, when placed in two locations <note>Presumably a reference to the specific visual grid or mathematical arrangement used in the manuscript's illustration for this chapter</note> according to the pattern of the holy Cross, it signifies the five books of the Law with the ten commandments; because everything that the Old Law depicted through figure and shadow, Christ fulfilled in truth through the Cross in the New Testament.

HEADER: BOOK TWO

Indeed, all things suit the Holy Cross most fittingly: both the shape of the letter and the number denoted within it, the mystery of the law and the sacrament of time, and the deed praiseworthily performed in this [sign]. Therefore, it is right that we all praise the Holy Cross with equal rejoicing, and give ineffable thanks to the crucified King, who by his own blood released all the debts of the world.

### Concerning the Twentieth Form, where the number one hundred and twenty is assigned.

<margin>20</margin>
Behold the pious shedding of Christ’s blood, and that wave which flowed from his side while he slept <note>A common patristic metaphor: Christ "sleeping" on the Cross refers to his death, just as Adam slept when Eve was formed from his side</note> upon the Cross; it cleanses us from all filth, because the Redeemer himself, by his death, took away all harmful things from us. He removed the stain of our sins and, through his passion, blotted out the <term>handwritten decree</term> <note>original: "chirographum"; a reference to Colossians 2:14, the "record of debt" or legal bond against humanity</note> that was set against us. He established the praiseworthy teaching of the Gospel, which, by putting to flight the darkness of sins, forbids every crime and utterly rejects the worship of idols. This teaching, showing us an honest life, commends itself to all nations under heaven through the power of virtues in its preachers. After the ascension of the Savior, the Apostles, having been instructed by Truth itself, testified as they preached the Gospel that the mysteries of the Old Testament were fulfilled and declared through Christ; they confirmed with true assertions that he is the end of the Law and the Prophets. 

Finally, the number 120 <note>original: "c x x."</note>—distinguished both in the age of the <term>lawgiver</term> <note>Moses, who died at age 120 (Deuteronomy 34:7)</note> and in the coming of the Holy Spirit upon the Apostles <note>Acts 1:15 notes there were about 120 believers gathered before Pentecost</note>—is nobly completed in the manner of a Cross by the letter <term>Lambda</term> <note>original: "lauda litera"; Hrabanus refers to the Greek letter Lambda (Λ), which represents the number 30. Placed four times (4 x 30 = 120), it forms the four arms of the Cross in his visual poem</note> being placed four times according to its significance. This reveals the sacraments of the faith and demonstrates the joys of true blessedness. For just as the Holy Cross collects 120 units into one through the four characters of the Lambda, so the Holy Spirit, arriving with the knowledge of all languages, united the 120 believers. From this, it is clearly and manifestly given to be understood that the Holy Cross is our true redemption, and that our unity truly consists within it. 

Therefore, having received the gift of speaking in all tongues, the joyful company of believers scattered the light of divine testimonies everywhere, while a multitude of miracles flashed forth. They cast the net of the Gospel into the sea of this world, so that the Lord's dragnet might pull men back from the depths of the abyss and bind them to the firmness of the Lord’s banner. Thus, the insignias of Christ’s Cross are open to all, showing how it assigns spiritual gifts to each of the faithful and makes them faithfully receive in heaven the rewards that the incarnate Savior promised them. These rewards are granted in increase according to the quality of one's merits; and the true guarantor, Christ the Son of God, together with God the Father and the Holy Spirit, preserves manifold rewards in the heights for those who are worthy. The King of Kings, reigning forever and governing all kingdoms by his own authority, truly grants these gifts. He gave us the Spirit, the <term>Paraclete</term> <note>the Comforter or Advocate</note>, as a pledge of our salvation and inheritance, so that by ruling us according to his will, he may preserve us until he makes us enter the joys of life with rejoicing. 

Sing psalms of life devoutly, sing well to the Lord Christ, all you nations, tribes, and every tongue, and recognize your true King, the wisdom and power of God the Father. By his power, death fell defeated and the memory of death was erased; recognize Jesus, the parent of all things. Because this praise is brought forth from a true and proven branch, it possesses an end and perfection in eternal rest. For this order is instilled in our nature: that it may serve the things spoken with reverence and trembling, and look forward to perpetual reward in the future. This is also our glory, this is and...

...virtue; this is the true stability of the highest rest, and he well preserves the laws of religion and uses his judgment rightly, who seeks the highest good above all things, and rules intermediate things rationally <note>These opening lines conclude the previous chapter's discussion on the proper balance of spiritual and worldly life</note>.

### Concerning the Twenty-First Figure, in which the number seventy-two is contained.

<margin>21</margin>
Therefore, the law of the Lord is true and blameless, written in the twenty-one books of the two testaments <note>The author likely uses a specific symbolic count for the divisions of the Old and New Testaments to match the figure number 21</note>; it must be placed in the figure of the Holy Cross. Through this Cross, the world has been released from its due wrath and has found eternal life and the harbor of salvation and eternal rest—namely, after that shipwreck which our first parent brought upon us through the transgression of the divine command. For because cruel death swallowed the whole human race through the <term>sin of gluttony</term> <note>original: "gulæ noxam"; a common medieval reference to Adam and Eve eating the forbidden fruit</note> involving the forbidden tree, and held us captive by its own right, it pleased our Redeemer to raise the wood of the Holy Cross upon the earth. This was done so that what that enemy had swallowed, he might now—being pierced by the point of the life-giving wood—vomit out through the grace of temperance. Thus, the enemy would pay the deserved penalties, because against all justice and all law, that most wicked servant and most deceitful thief had usurped dominion over the work of another. God, the author of all creation and the giver of the two testaments, wishing to make this most healthful work of the Holy Cross known, foretold it through the Law, promised it through the Prophets, and confesses through his Gospel that he has fulfilled it, so that humans might recognize their Creator and give thanks to their Redeemer.

Finally, the holy and magnificent Cross shows itself from this point entirely radiant with serene light; it demonstrates that it is the path and the guide to perpetual life for us. Therefore, like a lamp shining with the rays of eternal light, it calls all nations and peoples to the heavenly kingdoms. It proclaims that they have been mercifully rescued from the enemy, and thus it gladdens those of us now placed in the night of this world with its illumination, and afterwards elevates those who have earned it to the heights of heaven. There is no need to fear that any fallacy might deceive anyone, for the prince of this world having been cast out, the true Victress truly reigns. It is also for this reason that, in the preaching of its power and dominion, the holy preachers shine with miracles and subject the whole world to themselves. Through the grace of Christ, they make those who have been redeemed devout in heart, peaceful in character, gentle in patience, and tranquil in their way of life.

Behold how many languages of the nations there are: the Holy Cross is shown as a model in the number seventy-two <note>Ancient tradition held there were 72 distinct languages and nations following the Tower of Babel</note>, and through this, it signifies the open gate of light to all nations. The Savior himself ordered the <term>seventy-two disciples</term> to preach this, and he promised the company of the holy Archangels in heaven after the general resurrection—which this very number also designates. For the numbers eight and nine, when multiplied by each other, create seventy-two. Of these, the number eight relates to the time of the resurrection <note>The "eighth day" signifies the day of Christ's resurrection and the beginning of the new creation</note>, while the number nine refers to the <term>nine orders of Angels</term>. Thus, the Catholic faith holds that at the end of the world—that is, in the eighth age of the world—those rising shall pass into the fellowship of the Angels.

<margin>21</margin>
For Christ consumed all the sins of the world in the heat of his passion when, on the part of his flesh, he tasted death; through the power of his divinity, he liberated his chosen ones from the prison of hell. He commanded the light of sobriety and faith to be preached to the human race through his Apostles—namely, his Law, both Old and New. He demonstrated to all who believe in him that this Law, which accords with the figure of the Holy Cross, is a <term>light burden</term> and a <term>sweet yoke</term> <note>original: "leue onus atq; iugum ſuaue"; a reference to Matthew 11:30</note>, well-suited for leading one to the heavens.

BOOK TWO.

### Concerning the Twenty-Second Figure, in which the Monogram is depicted.

<margin>22</margin>
Christ, who is our true redeemer, in whom is all our desire, and who through His grace willed that I perform this work. O, would that He Himself be the end of my labor, and that He be the prize of my song <note>original: "pretium carminis"; the author views his writing as a musical or poetic offering to God</note>, to whom all good things are pleasing, because He Himself is the giver of all good things. Here He exhorts us, inviting all to heavenly gifts, and promises that these can be easily obtained if, having spurned all the desires of this world, one seeks them worthily through faith, hope, and charity. Indeed, when He came into this world and killed carnal love with the sword of <term>pious separation</term> <note>original: "piae separationis"; the spiritual detachment of the believer from worldly impulses</note>, He sowed these gifts through the preachers of His Gospel and sought the most peaceful fruit in His field. This is what the best Master always taught, forbidding His followers from turning toward low and downward paths; instead, He taught that they should lift themselves to arduous heights, and having understood His Gospel, lay aside their ingrained cruelty of character, learning to be mild and gentle. This is so that in His second advent, when He comes in the glory of His Father with His angels to render to each according to his works, He may find such people to whom, on account of their merits, He may give eternal rewards.

That number, which this <term>Monogram</term> <note>A symbolic arrangement of letters representing Christ, likely the Chi-Rho (XP)</note> represents in Greek letters, signifies both advents of the Lord Savior. That is, it signifies the first advent, when He was born upon the earth and cast out the prince of this world (specifically after His baptism), preaching the Gospel of the kingdom and healing every disease and every infirmity among the people. It also signifies the second advent, when the same just judge, the man Christ Jesus, shall descend from the throne of God the Father at the command and voice of the Archangel and with the trumpet of God. Then the dead who are in Christ shall rise to glory, according to the proclamation of the Holy Gospel and the voices of the Prophets, who testify that the saints of God will see the good things of the Lord in the land of the living, when they come and appear before the face of God.

Therefore, those who are of good merit then bring back the talents they received with profit to the Lord, and having been cleansed from every stain of sin (for they washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb), they earned the right to follow Him. They will sing a new song to God—namely, the angelic song <term>Alleluia</term> <note>A Hebrew expression of praise: "Praise the Lord"</note>—day and night in His holy temple. There will be no mourning or any pain there, because the first things have passed away, and all things will have been made new. Therefore, it is necessary that we strive to appease our God and Lord with full faith, which indeed works through love, so that He may then deign to become our helper and Savior when He comes to judgment according to the scriptures. Fire shall go before Him and set His enemies on fire round about; His ministers will come and gather all scandals out of His kingdom, and they will bind the <term>tares</term> <note>original: "Zizania"; weeds that resemble wheat, representing the wicked among the righteous</note> into bundles to be burned, but the wheat they will gather into the barn of their Lord.

O, exceedingly happy soul, who is permitted to enter the gates of heaven with an incorruptible body and to behold the Author of light with the pure eyes of the heart! Its desire will then be rightly fulfilled when it remains perfect in every part, and enjoys eternal joy with the holy Angelic Spirits in perennial light. By singing praises to Christ—truly singing a new song to the Lord in the assembly of the saints—it never learns to grow weary in that pursuit, because it thus desires to possess the kingdoms of heaven forever.

BOOK TWO. 11.

<margin>23</margin>
Behold, here shines this noble flower, painted with the name of the true King, that is, Jesus Christ; it is exemplified by the arms <note>original: "cornibus," literally 'horns,' often used to describe the four points or extremities of the Cross</note> of the holy Cross, demonstrating the joyful deeds of Christ. Therefore, the **number six** <note>original: "Senarius numerus"</note>, which the holy Cross marks through its individual arms arranged in a triple verse, designates the perfection of Christ's passion and our redemption. For just as the perfection of the world's creation is signified in the number six <note>referring to the six days of Creation in Genesis</note>, so also the perfect restoration of the world is implied through the number six, by Christ, who was crucified on the **sixth day** <note>original: "sexta feria"; Friday, the sixth day of the week</note>. Truly, that day was bright on which the Founder finished His work, and no less bright is this day on which the Redeemer sanctified His work by restoring it. Then, the Creator completed His creature by working, and now He has filled that same creature with heavenly blessing by repairing it.

Finally, to suggest the mystery, it happened that the number six, placed at the four arms of the Cross, extends through the four quarters of the world, demonstrating the perfection of things; for this is the first <term>perfect number</term> <note>In medieval mathematics, a "perfect number" is one equal to the sum of its divisors (1+2+3=6)</note>. It halves the <term>artificial day</term> <note>The "artificial day" was the 12 hours of daylight; six hours marks the midday point</note> and, when doubled, completes it. It is the sixth part of one month <note>30 days divided by 6 equals 5 days</note> and the sixtieth part of an entire year. It counts the leap-year quarter and joins the surplus with the five days; it ordains the <term>Ages of the World</term> <note>The "Six Ages of the World" (Sex aetates mundi) was a common medieval chronological framework</note> and will finish the course of time when the King of Kings shall come to forgive the sins of His saints with a peaceful countenance and hand over the heavenly kingdoms. 

Therefore, O good King Christ Jesus, You well know how to give certain rewards to Your servants, whom the true light of faith illuminating from all the world, and the living draught of wisdom refreshing them, has led to You, as they duly adorn themselves with the beauty of charity and works of justice. Finally, the aforementioned number placed around the Cross indicates the gathering of the peoples from the four quarters of the world to their Redeemer, praying to His divinity for eternal salvation, so that they may eagerly learn of His greatness from the perfect teaching of the Gospel, and prove their perfect faith through perfect works. Indeed, all the works of God are perfect, suggesting a perfect Creator, and they testify to His inestimable beauty by their own beauty. All things that are in the heavens, on the earth, and in the sea, praise the excellent Artisan. But let us humans, who are but a small part of His creation, sing—if not a worthy, then at least a devoted—glory to His name, and let us give thanks to Him for our redemption. For He who made and multiplied us has Himself freed us from the power of the enemy by His own blood. Thus, in this celebrated song, let us proclaim His love which He showed in us, because He demonstrated this by working with inestimable piety, suggested it by defending us, and commanded us to hold it by persuading us and showing that it is pleasing to Him.

### *Concerning the Twenty-Fourth Species, where the numbers one hundred, forty, and four are marked.*

<margin>24</margin>
O people beloved by God, O most holy order of virgins, bless the Lord Christ, singing to Him a **new song** which is [not] imitable by all others <note>A reference to Revelation 14:3, where the 144,000 sing a song that no one else could learn</note>. Sing the beauty of immortal glory before the throne of the Most High, and before the **four living creatures** <note>original: "4. animalia"; the winged beings of Ezekiel and Revelation</note> who are formed with diverse faces, and before the **twenty-four elders** sitting on twenty-four seats. You are those taken from humanity as the **first fruits** for God and the Lamb, beautiful cohorts purchased by the price of His blood; you stand in His camps and sing the most worthy praises of a most noble triumph. Your hand, playing upon the <term>citharas</term> <note>Ancient stringed instruments similar to lyres or harps</note>, renders the face of God serene and placid toward those born of earth, filling the halls of the house of the Lord with a powerful cry, even as the voice of great thunder peals in the ether, and as the voice of many waters resounds in the valleys. ...no lie was found, nor was there deceit in your heart; instead, fashioning pious songs, you sing worthy praises before the throne of God day and night, through the signs of virginity and the chastity of body and soul, which your King loves in you above all things. Therefore, most proven and perfect order of virgins—who, though of different sex and varying age, conducted a heavenly life in the world, remaining alien to every stain of fornication and immune to all the filth of the devil—sing praises to God through the duty of the mouth, the devotion of the heart, and the peaceful gesture of the body. Behold, your passage to heaven is made straight, where an eternal reward is prepared for you, where the immaculate Lamb of the Virgin feeds in flowery meadows.
